<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A cardinal $\lambda$ is called \emph{exacting} if for all ordinals $\alpha<\lambda<\zeta$, there is an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\zeta$ with $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ with $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\alpha=\operatorname{id}_\alpha$, $j\mathbin\upharpoonright \lambda\neq \operatorname{id}_{\lambda}$ and $j(\lambda)=\lambda$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
A cardinal $\lambda$ is called \emph{ultraexacting} if for all ordinals $\alpha<\lambda<\zeta$, there is an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\zeta$ with $V_\lambda\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ with $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\alpha=\operatorname{id}_\alpha$, $j\mathbin\upharpoonright \lambda\neq \operatorname{id}_{\lambda}$, $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda\in X$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- question-1: body_md -->
\label{Q01}
    Does $\textnormal{ZFC}$ prove the non-existence of exacting cardinals above an extendible cardinal?
<!-- end question-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm: a proper class of exactings}
   If there exists an I2-embedding, then there exists a transitive set-sized model of the theory $$\textnormal{ZFC} ~ + ~ "\textit{There is a proper class of exacting cardinals}".$$
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- question-2: body_md -->
\label{Q02}
    Does $\textnormal{ZFC}$ prove that a limit of exacting cardinals is not an exacting cardinal?
<!-- end question-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{theorem:ExactingLimit}
   If the Weak HOD Conjecture is true, then $\textnormal{ZFC}$ proves the following statements: 
   \begin{enumerate}
       \item\label{item:ExactingLimit1} A limit of
   exacting cardinals is not an exacting cardinal. 

       \item\label{item:ExactingLimit2} For every cardinal $\kappa$ of uncountable cofinality, there is a closed unbounded subset of $\kappa$ that does not contain an exacting cardinal.
   \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:SimplifiedConsStatLimitUltra}
        If $\textnormal{ZF}$ is consistent with the existence of a cardinal that is both supercompact and totally Reinhardt, then $\textnormal{ZFC}$ is consistent with the existence of a regular cardinal that is a stationary limit of ultraexacting cardinals.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- question-3: body_md -->
\label{Q03}
    Can small forcings create new exacting and ultraexacting cardinals?
<!-- end question-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{theorem:LevySolovayBeyondHOD}
  Let $\lambda$ be a cardinal and let ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$ be a partial order. 
  \begin{enumerate}
      \item\label{item:LevySolovayBeyondHOD1} If $\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}``\textit{$\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal }"$, then the following statements hold: 
       \begin{enumerate}
           \item If $\lambda$ has countable cofinality, then $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal. 

           \item If $\lambda$ has uncountable cofinality, then every closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ contains an exacting cardinal. 
       \end{enumerate}

        \item\label{item:LevySolovayBeyondHOD2} If $\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}``\textit{$\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }"$, then the following statements hold: 
       \begin{enumerate}
           \item If $\lambda$ has countable cofinality, then $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal. 

           \item If $\lambda$ has uncountable cofinality, then every closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ contains an ultraexacting cardinal. 
       \end{enumerate}
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{theorem: WeakHODConjecture and LevySolovay}
    If the Weak HOD Conjecture is true, then $\textnormal{ZFC}$ proves the following statements: 
  \begin{enumerate}
   \item The following statements are equivalent for every cardinal $\lambda$: 
     \begin{enumerate}
         \item $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal. 

        \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal }"$ holds for every partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$.   
        \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal }"$ holds for some partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$.   
     \end{enumerate}

    \item The following statements are equivalent for every cardinal $\lambda$: 
     \begin{enumerate}
         \item $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal. 

        \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }"$ holds for every partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$.   
        \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }"$ holds for some partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$.   
     \end{enumerate}
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- question-4: body_md -->
\label{Q04}
  If $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal, which of the following  statements holds in $\textnormal{HOD}$? 
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item $\lambda$ is a weakly compact cardinal. 

     \item $\lambda$ is a Woodin cardinal. 

     \item $\lambda$ is a limit of cardinals $\eta$ with the property that there exists an I3-embedding ${j}:{V_\eta}\longrightarrow{V_\eta}$. 
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end question-4 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{theorem:ExactingInHODIntro}
  If the Weak HOD Conjecture is true, then $\textnormal{ZFC}$ proves that the following statements hold for every exacting cardinal $\lambda$: 
  \begin{enumerate}
      \item\label{item:ExactingInHODIntro1} $\lambda$ is a Vop\v{e}nka cardinal in $\textnormal{HOD}$. 

      \item\label{item:ExactingInHODIntro2} In $\textnormal{HOD}$, for every closed unbounded subset $C$ of $\lambda$, there is  an I3-embedding whose critical sequence consists of elements of $C$.  
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{theorem: exacting + extendible} 
   If there exists an I2-embedding, then there exists a transitive  model of $\textnormal{ZF}$ with an exacting cardinal $\lambda$ such that $\lambda^+$ is extendible in $\textnormal{HOD}_x$ for every $x\subseteq\lambda$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:HODdichotomy}
    If \(\delta\) is an extendible cardinal then exactly one of the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item\label{item:HODclose} \(\textnormal{HOD}\) is a weak extender model for the supercompactness of \(\delta\).
        \item\label{item:HODfar} Every regular cardinal \(\kappa \geq \delta\) is \(\omega\)-strongly measurable in \(\textnormal{HOD}\).
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
There is a proper class of regular cardinals that are not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\hfill
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The \emph{$\textnormal{HOD}$ Conjecture} is the assertion that the theory
        $$\textnormal{ZFC}+\textit{``There is an extendible cardinal"}$$
        proves the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis. 
        
        \item The \emph{Weak $\textnormal{HOD}$ Conjecture} is the assertion that the theory
        $$\textnormal{ZFC}+\textit{``There is an extendible cardinal with a huge cardinal above"}$$
        proves the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{theorem:I2Char}
     The following statements are equivalent for every I3-embedding ${i}:{V_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}$: 
     \begin{enumerate}
        \item The embedding $i$ can be extended to an I2-embedding ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$. 

         \item If $R$ is a well-founded relation on $V_\lambda$, then $i_+(R)$ is a well-founded relation on $V_\lambda$. 
         
         \item The embedding $i$ is $\Sigma^1_1$-correct. 

         \item The embedding $i$ is $\Sigma^1_2$-correct.  
     \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{proposition:IterationFixedPoints}
If ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$ is an I2-embedding with critical point $\kappa$ and least non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$ that is given by a $(\kappa,\lambda)$-extender $E$ and  $$\langle\langle{M_\alpha}~\vert~{\alpha\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle,\langle{{j_{\alpha,\beta}}:{M_\alpha}\longrightarrow{M_\beta}}~\vert~{\alpha\leq\beta\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle\rangle$$ is the iteration of $V$ and $E$, then the following statements hold:  
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item\label{prop:InvEmb1} We  have $$x\in M_\omega ~ \Longleftrightarrow ~ j(x)\in M_\omega$$ for every set $x$ and $${j\mathbin\upharpoonright M_\omega}:{M_\omega}\longrightarrow{M_\omega}$$ is an elementary embedding. 

     \item\label{prop:InvEmb2} We have $$j(j_{0,\omega}(x)) ~ = ~ j_{0,\omega}(x)$$ for every set $x$. 
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
First, note that, in $V$, the above system of inner models and elementary embeddings is definable from the paramater $E$. 
   
  In addition, the system  $$\langle\langle{M_{1+\alpha}}~\vert~{\alpha\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle,\langle{{j_{1+\alpha,1+\beta}}:{M_{1+\alpha}}\longrightarrow{M_{1+\beta}}}~\vert~{\alpha\leq\beta\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle\rangle$$ is the iteration of $M_1$ and $j(E)$, and this system is definable in $M_1$ by the same formulas and the parameter $j(E)$. 
   
  Given $\alpha\leq\omega$, this shows that  $$x\in M_\alpha ~ \Longleftrightarrow ~ j(x)\in M_{1+\alpha}$$ holds for every set $x$ and $${j\mathbin\upharpoonright M_\alpha}:{M_\alpha}\longrightarrow{M_{1+\alpha}}$$ is an elementary embedding. This directly implies \eqref{prop:InvEmb1}. In addition, given $\alpha\leq\beta\leq\omega$, we have   $$j(j_{\alpha,\beta}(x)) ~ = ~ j_{1+\alpha,1+\beta}(j(x))$$  for every $x\in M_\alpha$. Since $j_{1,\omega}\circ j=j_{0,\omega}$, this directly implies \eqref{prop:InvEmb2}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lemma:I2andVHOD}
    If the $\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds and ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$ is an I2-embedding with critical point $\kappa$ and least non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$ that is induced by a $(\kappa,\lambda)$-extender, then there is a cofinality-preserving generic extension $V[G]$ such that $j$ lifts to an I2-embedding in $V[G]$ and $``V=\textnormal{gHOD}$" holds in $V[G]_\lambda$.

    Moreover, $\mathrm{CCA}$ holds in $V[G]_\lambda$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{I}\subseteq \lambda$ denote the set of all inaccessible cardinals less than $\lambda$. Let $${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda  ~ = ~ \langle{{\mathbb{P}}_\alpha;\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}_\alpha}~\vert~{\alpha<\lambda}\rangle$$ denote the Easton support  forcing iteration that is non-trivial only at those   $\min(\mathcal{I})<\alpha\in\mathcal{I}$ such that $\sup(\mathcal{I}\cap \alpha)<\alpha$ holds, in which case ${\mathbb{P}}_\alpha$ forces $\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}_\alpha$ to be the canonical ${<}\sup(\mathcal{I}\cap \kappa)^+$-directed-closed forcing coding $V[\dot{G}]_\alpha$ into the continuum pattern of $V[\dot{G}]_\alpha$ (see \cite{McAloon}). 
  
 Then ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$ is $\sigma$-closed and, since the $\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds in the ground model, standard arguments (see {\cite[Section 7]{CummingsHandbook}})  show that forcing with ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$ preserves all cofinalities. Moreover, the above definition ensures that $V[H]_\lambda$  satisfy $``V=\textnormal{gHOD}$" whenever $H$ is $\mathbb{P}_\lambda$-generic over $V$.
  
 Therefore, it suffices to check that ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$ lifts to an I2-embedding in some $\mathbb{P}_\lambda$-generic extension of $V$. 


 Let $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j$. Then $\kappa_0$ is the critical point of $j$ and $\lambda=\sup_{n<\omega}\kappa_n$. 
 Since  the partial order ${\mathbb{P}}_\alpha$ is uniformly definable in $V_\lambda$ from the parameter $\alpha<\lambda$, it follows that $j({\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n})={\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ and $j({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})})={\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}$ for all $n<\omega$. This shows that $j[{\mathbb{P}}_\lambda]$ is a subset of ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$. 
  
  Given $n<\omega$, it is also obvious that $|\mathbb{P}_\alpha|<\kappa_n$ holds for all $\alpha<\kappa_n$ and every condition in $\mathbb{P}_{\kappa_n}$ forces $\mathbb{P}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}$ to be ${<}\kappa_n^+$-directed closed. 
   
                                                                                                                                                                     


\begin{claim*}
  Let $n<\omega$, let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$-generic over $V$, let $\bar{G}$ be the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ induced by $G$ and let $H$ be the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ induced by $G$. If $j[\bar{G}]\subseteq G$ holds and  ${j_*}:{V[\bar{G}]}\longrightarrow{M[G]}$ is the corresponding lifting of $j$, then $j_*[H]$ is a subset of ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$ with a lower bound. 
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
\end{claim*}

\begin{proof}[Proof of claim]
  First, note that, since $\kappa_{n+1}$ is an inaccessible limit of inaccessible cardinals and ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$ has Easton support, it follows that ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ has cardinality at most $\kappa_{n+1}$ in $V$ and ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ has cardinality at most $\kappa_{n+1}$ in $V[G]$. In particular, we know that $H$ has cardinality at most $\kappa_{n+1}$ in $V[G]$. 
   
  Since $j({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}) =  {\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}$, we also know that $$j_*[H] ~ \subseteq ~ j_*({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}) ~ = ~ {\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G.$$ Finally, since $j_*$ is an elementary embedding, the directedness of $H$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ implies the directedness of $j_*[H]$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$. 
   
  The statement of the claim now follows from the earlier observation that ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$ is ${<}\kappa_{n+1}^+$-directed closed in $V[G]$. 
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
\end{proof}


 We  now use this claim to inductively construct a sequence $\langle{p_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ consisting of conditions $p_n$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ satisfying the following statements: 
   \begin{enumerate}
       \item If $m<n<\omega$, then $p_n\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{m+1}\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{m+1}}}p_m$. 

       \item If $n<\omega$, $G$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$-generic over $V$ with $p_n\in G$, $\bar{G}$ is the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ induced by $G$ and $H$ is the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ induced by $G$, then $j[\bar{G}]\subseteq G$ and $p_{n+1}\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})$ is a lower bound of $j_*[H]$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$, where ${j_*}:{V[\bar{G}]}\longrightarrow{M[G]}$ is the canonical lifting of $j$. 
   \end{enumerate}
 
 First, define $p_0$ to be the trivial condition in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_1}$. Since $j\mathbin\upharpoonright{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_0}=\operatorname{id}_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_0}}$ and ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_0}$ is a direct limit, we obviously have $j[\bar{G}]\subseteq G$ whenever $G$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_1}$-generic over $V$ and $\bar{G}$ is the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_0}$ induced by $G$. 
  
 Now, assume that $n<\omega$ and there exists a condition $p_n$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ with the desired properties. By the above claim, these properties ensure that there is a ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$-name $\dot{q}$ for a condition in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}$ with the property that whenever $G$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$-generic over $V$ with $p_n\in G$,  $\bar{G}$ is the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ induced by $G$,  $H$ is the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ induced by $G$ and ${j_*}:{V[\bar{G}]}\longrightarrow{M[G]}$ is the canonical lifting of $j$ enabled by the fact that $j[\bar{G}]\subseteq G$ holds, then $\dot{q}^G$ is a lower bound of $j_*[H]$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$. 
  
 Define $p_{n+1}$ to be a condition in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+2}}$ that gets mapped below $\langle p_n,\dot{q}\rangle$ by the canonical dense embedding of ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+2}}$ into ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}*{\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}$. 
  
 Then $p_{n+1}\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}}p_n$ and $p_{n+1}\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})$ is a lower bound of $j_*[H]$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$, whenever $G$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$-generic over $V$ with $p_n\in G$, $\bar{G}$ is the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ induced by $G$, $H$ is the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ induced by $G$ and ${j_*}:{V[\bar{G}]}\longrightarrow{M[G]}$ is the corresponding lifting of $j$. 
  
 Finally, let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+2}}$-generic over $V$ with $p_{n+1}\in G$ and let $\bar{G}$ be the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ induced by $G$. Fix a condition $q$ in $\bar{G}$. Since $p_n$ is an element of $\bar{G}$, we know that $j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}=j(q\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n)\in\bar{G}$. Moreover, our construction also ensures that 
 \begin{equation*}
   \begin{split}
       p_{n+1}\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2}) ~ & \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G} ~ \dot{q}^G \\ & \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G} ~ j(q\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})) ~ = ~ j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2}).
   \end{split}
 \end{equation*}
 This shows that there is a condition $r\in G$ with $r\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+2}}}j(q)$. In particular, we know that $j[\bar{G}]\subseteq G$ holds in this case. 


 Since all of the partial orders in our iteration are countably closed, we can now find a condition $p$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$ satisfying $p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}}p_n$ for all $n<\omega$. Let $F$ be ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$-generic over $V$ with $p\in F$ and assume, towards a contradiction, that there is a condition $q$ in $F$ with $j(q)\notin F$. Let $r$ be a common strengthening of $p$ and $q$ in $F$. Then $r\not\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_\lambda}j(q)$ and we can find a minimal $n<\omega$ with the property that $$r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1} ~ \not\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}} ~ j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1} ~ = ~ j(q\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n).$$ We then know $n>0$, because $r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_0\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_0}}q\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_0$ and Easton support ensures that $j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_0,\kappa_1)$ is the trivial condition in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_0,\kappa_1)}$. 
  
  The minimality of $n$ then ensures that $r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}} j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n$ and there exists a filter $G$ on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ that is generic over $V$, contains $r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n$ and has the property that $r\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})$ is not a strengthening of $j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^G$. 
   
  Let $\bar{G}$ denote the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n-1}}$ induced by $G$ and let $H$ denote the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n-1},\kappa_n)}^{\bar{G}}$ induced by $G$.   Since $p_{n-1}$ is an element of $G$, we have $j[\bar{G}]\subseteq G$  and  $p_n\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})$ is a lower bound of $j_*[H]$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^G$, where ${j_*}:{V[\bar{G}]}\longrightarrow{M[G]}$ is the canonical lifting of $j$. Moreover, since $q\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n$ is an element of $G$ and therefore $q\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n-1},\kappa_n)$ is an element of $H$, it follows that the condition $j(q\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n-1},\kappa_n))=j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})$ is an element of $j_*[H]$. In combination, this shows that $$r\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1}) ~ \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^G} ~ j(q)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1}),$$ a contradiction. 
   
  These computations show that $j[F]$ is contained in $F$. 


  Given $\ell<\omega$, we let $F_\ell$ denote the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_\ell}$ induced by $F$. Define $\bar{F}$ to be the set of all conditions $p$ in $j({\mathbb{P}}_\lambda)$ with the property that there exists $n<\omega$, $q\in F_{n+1}$ and $r\in F$ such that $$\langle q,j(r)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\lambda)\rangle ~ \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}*j({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)})}} ~ \langle p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}, ~ p\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\lambda)\rangle$$ holds in $M$. 
   
  The fact that $j[F]$ is a subset of $F$ then implies that $\bar{F}$ is a filter on $j({\mathbb{P}}_\lambda)$ that contains $j[F]$. 
  

  \begin{claim*}
    $\bar{F}$ is $j({\mathbb{P}}_\lambda)$-generic over $M$. 
  \end{claim*}

  \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
    Let $D$ be a dense open subset of $j({\mathbb{P}}_\lambda)$ in $M$. Since $M$ is an ultrapower of $V$ using a $(\kappa,\lambda)$-extender, we can find a function $f$ with domain $V_\lambda$ and $y\in V_\lambda$ with  $j(f)(y)=D$ (see e.g., \cite[\S3]{PovTwo}). We may assume that $f(x)$ is a dense open subset of ${\mathbb{P}}$ for every $x\in V_\lambda$. 
     
    Fix $n<\omega$ with $y\in V_{\kappa_{n+1}}$. 
     
    It is then easy to see that $$\{{p\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\lambda)}~\vert~{p\in f(x), ~ p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n\in F}\}$$ is a dense subset of ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)}^{F_n}$ in $V[F_n]$ for every $x\in V_\lambda$. 
     
    Since $V_{\kappa_n}$ has cardinality $\kappa_n$ in the ground model and ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)}^{F_n}$ is ${<}\kappa_n^+$-directed closed in $V[F_n]$, we can find a condition $r$ in $F$ with the property that for every $x\in V_{\kappa_n}$, the set of conditions $q$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ with the property that there exists $p\in f(x)$ with $$\langle q, ~  r\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\lambda)\rangle ~ \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}*{\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)}} ~ \langle p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n, ~ p\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\lambda)\rangle$$
    is dense below $r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$. 
     
    Elementarity now implies that, in $M$, the set of conditions $q$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ with the property that there exists $p\in D$ with 
    \begin{equation}\label{equation:DenseInUltrapower}
        \langle q, ~  j(r)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\lambda)\rangle ~ \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}*j({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)})} ~ \langle p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}, ~ p\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\lambda)\rangle
    \end{equation}
    is dense below $j(r)\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$. 
     
    Since the above computations show that $j(r)\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}=j(r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n)\in F$, we can find  $q\in F_{n+1}$ and $p\in D$ such that \eqref{equation:DenseInUltrapower} holds. Then $p$ is an element of $D\cap\bar{F}$.  
  \end{proof}


  The above claim shows that we can lift $j$ to an elementary embedding  $${j}:{V[F]}\longrightarrow{M[\bar{F}]}.$$ 
  
  
  \begin{claim*}
      $V[F]_\lambda\subseteq M[\bar{F}]$. 
  \end{claim*}

  \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
    Fix $n<\omega$ and $x\in V[F]_{\kappa_n}$. The definition of ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$ then ensures that $x$ is of the form $\tau^{F_n}$ for some ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$-name $\tau$ in $V_\lambda$. By the definition of $\bar{F}$, we now have  $F_n\in M[\bar{F}]$ and hence $x\in M[\bar{F}]$. 
  \end{proof}

  We now know that $j$ lifts to an I2-embedding in $V[F]$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- claim--1: body_md -->
Let $n<\omega$, let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$-generic over $V$, let $\bar{G}$ be the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ induced by $G$ and let $H$ be the filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ induced by $G$. If $j[\bar{G}]\subseteq G$ holds and  ${j_*}:{V[\bar{G}]}\longrightarrow{M[G]}$ is the corresponding lifting of $j$, then $j_*[H]$ is a subset of ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$ with a lower bound.
<!-- end claim--1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
First, note that, since $\kappa_{n+1}$ is an inaccessible limit of inaccessible cardinals and ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$ has Easton support, it follows that ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ has cardinality at most $\kappa_{n+1}$ in $V$ and ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ has cardinality at most $\kappa_{n+1}$ in $V[G]$. In particular, we know that $H$ has cardinality at most $\kappa_{n+1}$ in $V[G]$. 
   
  Since $j({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}) =  {\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}$, we also know that $$j_*[H] ~ \subseteq ~ j_*({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}) ~ = ~ {\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G.$$ Finally, since $j_*$ is an elementary embedding, the directedness of $H$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})}^{\bar{G}}$ implies the directedness of $j_*[H]$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$. 
   
  The statement of the claim now follows from the earlier observation that ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_{n+1},\kappa_{n+2})}^G$ is ${<}\kappa_{n+1}^+$-directed closed in $V[G]$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- claim--2: body_md -->
$\bar{F}$ is $j({\mathbb{P}}_\lambda)$-generic over $M$.
<!-- end claim--2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $D$ be a dense open subset of $j({\mathbb{P}}_\lambda)$ in $M$. Since $M$ is an ultrapower of $V$ using a $(\kappa,\lambda)$-extender, we can find a function $f$ with domain $V_\lambda$ and $y\in V_\lambda$ with  $j(f)(y)=D$ (see e.g., \cite[\S3]{PovTwo}). We may assume that $f(x)$ is a dense open subset of ${\mathbb{P}}$ for every $x\in V_\lambda$. 
     
    Fix $n<\omega$ with $y\in V_{\kappa_{n+1}}$. 
     
    It is then easy to see that $$\{{p\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\lambda)}~\vert~{p\in f(x), ~ p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n\in F}\}$$ is a dense subset of ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)}^{F_n}$ in $V[F_n]$ for every $x\in V_\lambda$. 
     
    Since $V_{\kappa_n}$ has cardinality $\kappa_n$ in the ground model and ${\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)}^{F_n}$ is ${<}\kappa_n^+$-directed closed in $V[F_n]$, we can find a condition $r$ in $F$ with the property that for every $x\in V_{\kappa_n}$, the set of conditions $q$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$ with the property that there exists $p\in f(x)$ with $$\langle q, ~  r\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\lambda)\rangle ~ \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}*{\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)}} ~ \langle p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n, ~ p\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_n,\lambda)\rangle$$
    is dense below $r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$. 
     
    Elementarity now implies that, in $M$, the set of conditions $q$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$ with the property that there exists $p\in D$ with 
    \begin{equation}\label{equation:DenseInUltrapower}
        \langle q, ~  j(r)\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\lambda)\rangle ~ \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}*j({\mathbb{P}}_{[\kappa_n,\lambda)})} ~ \langle p\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}, ~ p\mathbin\upharpoonright[\kappa_{n+1},\lambda)\rangle
    \end{equation}
    is dense below $j(r)\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_{n+1}}$. 
     
    Since the above computations show that $j(r)\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_{n+1}=j(r\mathbin\upharpoonright\kappa_n)\in F$, we can find  $q\in F_{n+1}$ and $p\in D$ such that \eqref{equation:DenseInUltrapower} holds. Then $p$ is an element of $D\cap\bar{F}$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->

$V[F]_\lambda\subseteq M[\bar{F}]$.
<!-- end claim--3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Fix $n<\omega$ and $x\in V[F]_{\kappa_n}$. The definition of ${\mathbb{P}}_\lambda$ then ensures that $x$ is of the form $\tau^{F_n}$ for some ${\mathbb{P}}_{\kappa_n}$-name $\tau$ in $V_\lambda$. By the definition of $\bar{F}$, we now have  $F_n\in M[\bar{F}]$ and hence $x\in M[\bar{F}]$.
