<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemma:CharExactingSingleEmb}
   A cardinal $\lambda$ is exacting if and only if there exists   $\lambda<\eta\in C^{(1)}$,   $\lambda<\zeta\in C^{(2)}$, an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\eta$ with $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ satisfying $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$ and $j(\lambda)=\lambda$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
A cardinal $\lambda$ is ultraexacting if and only if there exists $\lambda<\eta\in C^{(1)}$, $\lambda<\zeta\in C^{(2)}$, an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\eta$ with $V_\lambda\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ satisfying $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$, $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda\in X$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{fact:CharExacting}
    A cardinal $\lambda$ is exacting if and only if for every ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$, there are $x,y\in A$ and a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle}\longrightarrow{\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)<\lambda$.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{fact:CharUltraexacting}
    A cardinal $\lambda$ is ultraexacting if and only if for every ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$, there is a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle}\longrightarrow{\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)<\lambda$.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lemma:ExactingSmallForcing}
 Let $\lambda$ be a cardinal and ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$ be a partial order. 
  \begin{enumerate}
      \item\label{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing1} If $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal, then $$\mathbbm{1}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\check{\lambda}$ is an exacting cardinal }".$$ 

      \item\label{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing2} If $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal, then $$\mathbbm{1}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\check{\lambda}$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }".$$
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
\eqref{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing1} Pick $\lambda<\zeta\in C^{(3)}$ and an inaccessible cardinal $\delta<\lambda$ with ${\mathbb{P}}\in V_\delta$. We can now use our assumption to find an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\zeta$ with $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ with $j\mathbin\upharpoonright \delta=\operatorname{id}_\delta$, $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$. 
    
   Let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}$-generic over $V$. Since $\mathcal{P}({\mathbb{P}})^V\subseteq X$, it follows that the set $$X[G] ~ = ~ \{{\tau^G}~\vert~{\textit{$\tau\in X$ is a ${\mathbb{P}}$-name}}\}$$ is an elementary submodel of $V[G]_\zeta$ and the embedding $j$ can be extended to ${j_G}:{X[G]}\longrightarrow{V[G]_\zeta}$. 
    
   Since the partial order ${\mathbb{P}}$ is an element of $V_\zeta$, it follows that $\zeta$ is an element of $(C^{(3)})^{V[G]}$ and, by Lemma \ref{lemma:CharExactingSingleEmb}, this shows that the embedding $j_G$ witnesses that $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $V[G]$. 

   \eqref{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing2} Pick $\delta$, $\zeta$, $X$ and $j$ satisfying the statements listed in \eqref{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing1} and the additional assumption that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda$ is an element of $X$. Then $X$ contains a ${\mathbb{P}}$-name for the canonical lifting of $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda$ to the $V_\lambda$ of ${\mathbb{P}}$-generic extensions. Combined with the argument in \eqref{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing1}, this shows that ${\mathbb{P}}$-forces $\lambda$ to be an ultraexacting cardinal.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:ZFinaccessible}
    A cardinal $\kappa$ is \emph{strongly inaccessible} if  for each  $\alpha<\kappa$, there is no  ${f}:{V_\alpha}\longrightarrow{\kappa}$ whose range is unbounded in $\kappa$.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:ZFsupercompact}
 A cardinal $\kappa$ is  \emph{supercompact} if for every $\eta>\kappa$, there is $\zeta>\eta$, a transitive set $N$ with ${}^{V_\eta}N\subseteq N$ and a non-trivial embedding ${j}:{V_\zeta}\longrightarrow{N}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\kappa$ and $j(\kappa)>\eta$.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
A cardinal $\lambda$ is \emph{exacting} if for every non-empty ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$, there exist $x,y\in A$ and a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle}\longrightarrow{\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)<\lambda$.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
\label{definition:ZFultraexacting} 
    A cardinal $\lambda$ is \emph{ultraexacting} if for every ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$, there is a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle}\longrightarrow{\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)<\lambda$.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:ZFExactingDown}\label{prop:ExactingRankSegments}
  Let $\delta$ be an ordinal such that $V_\delta$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZF}$. 
   \begin{enumerate}
       \item If $\lambda<\delta$ is an exacting cardinal, then $\lambda$ is  exacting  in $V_\delta$. 

       \item If $\lambda<\delta$ is an ultraexacting cardinal, then $\lambda$ is  ultraexacting  in $V_\delta$. 
   \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Both statements follow directly from the above definitions using the fact that every element in $\textnormal{OD}^{V_\delta}$ is ordinal definable in $V$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:ExactingDownToL}
    Let $\lambda$ be a cardinal and let $\xi>\lambda$ be an ordinal. 
       \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{prop:ZFexactL1} If $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal, then $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $L(V_\xi)$. 

        \item\label{prop:ZFexactL2} If $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal, then $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $L(V_\xi)$. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
\eqref{prop:ZFexactL1} Let $A$ be a subset of $V_{\lambda+1}$ that is ordinal definable in $L(V_\xi)$. 
     
    Then $A$ is ordinal definable in $V$ and there exist $x,y\in A$ with the property that there exists a non-trivial elementary embedding  of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$ in $V$ and this map is also an element of $L(V_\xi)$. Hence, $L(V_\xi)\models\lambda$ is exacting.
    
   \eqref{prop:ZFexactL2} Let $A$ be a subset of $V_{\lambda+1}$ that is ordinal definable in $L(V_\xi)$. Then $A$ is ordinal definable in $V$ and there exists a non-trivial elementary embedding $j$ of $\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle$ into itself. Then $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda$ is an element of $L(V_\xi)$ and, since $\lambda$ is a limit ordinal, it follows that the map $j$ is also contained in $L(V_\xi)$. We can now conclude that $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $L(V_\xi)$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:PreserveExactingGoodForcing}
    Let $\lambda$ be a cardinal and let ${\mathbb{P}}$ be an ordinal definable,  weakly homogeneous partial order with the property that forcing with ${\mathbb{P}}$ does not add new subsets of $V_\lambda$. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{prop:ZFforcingPreserve1} If $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal, then $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in every ${\mathbb{P}}$-generic extension. 

        \item\label{prop:ZFforcingPreserve2} If $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal, then $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in every ${\mathbb{P}}$-generic extension. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
\eqref{prop:ZFforcingPreserve1} Let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}$-generic over $V$ and let $A$ be a subset of $V[G]_{\lambda+1}$ that is ordinal definable in $V[G]$. Then $A$ consists of elements of $V$ and the weak homogeneity of ${\mathbb{P}}$ allows us to conclude that $A$ is an element of the ground model $V$. Since ${\mathbb{P}}$ is ordinal definable in $V$, we now know that $A$ is also ordinal definable in $V$. Moreover, the fact that $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $V$ allows us to find $x,y\in A$ with the property that there exists a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$ in $V$. By our assumptions, this map is also a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V[G]_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V[G]_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$. These computations show that $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $V[G]$. 

 
 \eqref{prop:ZFforcingPreserve2} Let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}$-generic over $V$ and let $A$ be a subset of $V[G]_{\lambda+1}$ that is ordinal definable in $V[G]$. As above, it follows that $A$ is an ordinal definable element of the ground model $V$. Therefore, ultraexactingness yields a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle$ into itself. Since $V_{\lambda+1}=V[G]_{\lambda+1}$, this map is also a non-trivial elementary embedding of  $\langle V[G]_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle$ into itself. This shows that $\lambda$ is ultraexacting in $V[G]$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{theorem:ExactingInnerModels}
  Let $\lambda$ be singular cardinal of countable cofinality and let $N$ be (possibly class-sized) transitive model of $\textnormal{ZF}$  such that $V_\lambda\in N$, ${{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N=\omega$ and there is a well-ordering of $V_\lambda$ in $N$. 
   
  If there are subclasses $X_0$ and $X_1$ of $N$ that contain $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}$ and are $\Sigma_2$-correct in $N$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X_0}\longrightarrow{X_1}$ with $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$ and $j(\lambda)=\lambda$, then $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $N$.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Assume, towards a contradiction, that $\lambda$ is not an exacting cardinal in $N$. By definition, this means that, in $N$, there is a non-empty ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$ with the property that for all $x,y\in A$, there is no non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$. 
      
     Using the $\Sigma_2$-definability of the class of proper initial segments of the canonical wellordering of ordinal definable sets (see {\cite[Proposition 3.9]{Sigma1Partitions}}), we can find a non-empty subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$ in $N$ with the property that, in $N$, the set $\{A\}$ is definable by a $\Sigma_2$-formula with parameter $\lambda$ and for all $x,y\in A$, there is no non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$. 
      
     The $\Sigma_2$-correctness of $X$ in $N$ then ensures that $A$ is an element of $X_0\cap X_1$ with $A\cap X_0\neq\emptyset$ and $j(A)=A$. Pick $x\in A\cap X_0$ and set $y=j(x)\in A$. Since $V_\lambda$ is an element of $X_0$ with $j(V_\lambda)=V_\lambda$, it follows that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda$ is a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$. 
     
     
     Now, fix a  sequence $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ in $N$ that is cofinal in $\lambda$ and satisfies $j(\kappa_0)>\kappa_0$. 
      
     Define $T$ to be the set of all partial non-trivial elementary embeddings $i$ of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$ such that $i$ is an element of $V_\lambda$, $\mathop{\mathrm{dom}}\nolimits(i)=V_{\kappa_n}\cup\{\kappa_n\}$ for some $n<\omega$ and $i(\kappa_0)>\kappa_0$. 
      
     Then $T$ is an element of $N$ and, if we order $T$ by end-extensions of functions, then we turn this set into a tree of height at most $\omega$.  For each $n<\omega$, the restriction $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(V_{\kappa_n}\cup\{\kappa_n\})$ is an element of $T$. 
      
     It follows that $T$ has height $\omega$ and is ill-founded in $V$. 
      
                                                   
      
     Fix a well-ordering $\lhd$ of $V_\lambda$ in $N$. Since $T$ is a subset of $V_\lambda$, the ill-foundedness of $T$ in $V$ ensures the existence of a unique $\lhd$-leftmost branch $b_\lhd$ through $T$. It then follows that  $b_\lhd$ is an element of $N$ and $\bigcup b$ is a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$ in $N$, contradicting our choice of $A$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{corollary:ExactingInnerModel}
    Let ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$ be a non-trivial elementary embedding with first non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$. Assume that $N\subseteq M$ is a (possibly class-sized) transitive model of $\textnormal{ZF}$ such that $V_\lambda\in N$, ${{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N=\omega$ and there is a well-ordering of $V_\lambda$ in $N$.    
     
    If   $j\mathbin\upharpoonright N$ is an elementary embedding of $N$ into $N$, then $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $N$.  \qed
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{corollary:ExactingModels}
    Let ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$ be an I2-embedding with critical sequence  $\vec{\kappa}=\langle{\kappa_m}~\vert~{m<\omega}\rangle$ and first non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$ that is given by a $(\kappa_0,\lambda)$-extender $E$. Let $U$ denote the ultrafilter on $\kappa$ induced by $j$ and let $\langle{M_\alpha}~\vert~{\alpha\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle$ denote  the sequence of inner models obtained by iterating $V$ and $E$. 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{item:ExactingModels1} The sequence $\vec{\kappa}$ is generic over $M_\omega$ and $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $M_\omega[\vec{\kappa}]$. 

        \item\label{item:ExactingModels2} If ${\mathbb{P}}_U$ is the Prikry forcing using $U$, then ${\mathbb{P}}_U$ forces $\kappa$ to be an exacting cardinal. 

        \item\label{item:ExactingModels3} The class $\bigcap_{n<\omega} M_n$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZF}$ and $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $\bigcap_{n<\omega} M_n$. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
\eqref{item:ExactingModels1} Standard arguments show that the sequence $\vec{x}$ induces a generic filter for the Prikry forcing in $M_\omega$ that uses the image of $U$ under the canonical embedding of $V$ into $M_\omega$. Moreover, it is easy to show that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright M_\omega$ is an elementary embedding of $M_\omega$ into itself. Since $j(\vec{\kappa})=\langle{\kappa_{m+1}}~\vert~{m<\omega}\rangle$ and therefore $M_\omega[\vec{\kappa}]=M_\omega[j(\vec{\kappa})]$, it follows that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright M_\omega[\vec{\kappa}]$ is an elementary embedding of $M_\omega[\vec{\kappa}]$ into itself. Finally, since $M_\omega[\vec{\kappa}]$ is an inner model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$ containing $V_\lambda$ and $\vec{\kappa}$ is cofinal in $\lambda$, we can apply Corollary \ref{corollary:ExactingInnerModel} to conclude that $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $M_\omega[\vec{\kappa}]$. 

  \eqref{item:ExactingModels2} Using the elementarity of the canonical embedding of $V$ into $M_\omega$, the given statement follows directly from the above proof of \eqref{item:ExactingModels1}.
  
  \eqref{item:ExactingModels3}  Set $N=\bigcap_{n<\omega} M_n$. Standard arguments then show that $N$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZF}$ that contains $M_\omega$. In particular, it follows that $V_\lambda$ is contained in $N$ and there is a well-ordering of $V_\lambda$ in $N$. Moreover, it is easy to see that the sequence $\vec{\kappa}$ is an element of $N$ and therefore $\lambda$ has countable cofinality in $N$. The desired conclusion now follows from Corollary \ref{corollary:ExactingInnerModel}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{theorem:UltraexactingInnerModels}
  Let $\lambda$ be singular cardinal and let $N$ be (possibly class-sized) transitive model of $\textnormal{ZF}$  with the property that  $V_\lambda\in N$ and $\lambda$ is singular in $N$. 
   
  If there are subclasses $X_0$ and $X_1$ of $N$ that contain $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}$ and are $\Sigma_2$-correct in $N$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X_0}\longrightarrow{X_1}$ with $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$, $j\mathbin\upharpoonright{{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N=\operatorname{id}_{{{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N}$,  $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda\in X_0$, then $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $N$.
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Assume, towards a contradition, that $\lambda$ is not an ultraexacting cardinal in $N$. Then, in $N$, there is an ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$ with the property that  there is no non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ into itself. 
      
     By using the canonical well-ordering of ordinal definable sets, we can find a subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$ in $N$ with the property that, in $N$, the set $\{A\}$ is definable by a $\Sigma_2$-formula with parameter $\lambda$ and  there is no non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ into itself. 
      
     The correctness properties of $X_0$ and $X_1$  now imply that $A\in X_0\cap X_1$ and $j(A)=A$. 

     Next, we can find  a  sequence $\langle{\kappa_\gamma}~\vert~{\gamma<{{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N}\rangle$ in $X_0$ that is cofinal in $\lambda$. Define $${i}:{V_{\lambda+1}^N}\longrightarrow{V_{\lambda+1}^N}; ~ x\mapsto\bigcup\{{(j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda)(x\cap V_{\kappa_\gamma})}~\vert~{\gamma<{{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N}\}.$$ Then $i$ is an element of $X_0$ and therefore $i[V_{\lambda+1}\cap X_0]\subseteq X_0$. Moreover, since $j(\lambda)=\lambda$, it follows that $j({{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N)={{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N$ and therefore we have   
     $$j\mathbin\upharpoonright({{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N+1) ~ = ~ \operatorname{id}_{{{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N+1}.$$ Since this directly implies that $$i\mathbin\upharpoonright(V_{\lambda+1}\cap X_0) ~ = ~ j\mathbin\upharpoonright(V_{\lambda+1}\cap X_0),$$ we can conclude that $i$ is a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ into itself in $X_0$. The correctness properties of $X_0$ in $N$ now ensure that $i$ is a function with these properties in $N$, contradicting our choice of $A$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
A \emph{Reinhardt embedding} is a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{V}$. A \emph{Reinhardt cardinal} is the critical point of a Reinhardt embedding.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
A cardinal $\lambda$ is \emph{rank-Berkeley} if for all ordinals $\alpha<\lambda<\zeta$, there is a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{V_\zeta}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ such that $\alpha<\operatorname{crit}(j)<\lambda$ and $\lambda$ is the first non-trivial fixed point of $j$.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:LocalRankBerkeleySupercompact}
    If $\delta$ is a supercompact cardinal and $\lambda<\delta$ is rank-Berkeley in $V_\delta$, then $\lambda$ is rank-Berkeley.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Fix an ordinal $\eta\geq\delta$. Then there is $\zeta>\eta$, a transitive set $N$ with ${}^{V_\eta}N\subseteq N$ and a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{V_\zeta}\longrightarrow{N}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\delta$ and $j(\delta)>\eta$. Since $\lambda$ is rank-Berkeley in $j(V_\delta)$ and $V_\eta\in N$, there exists an elementary embedding ${i}:{V_\eta}\longrightarrow{V_\eta}$ with critical point below $\lambda$ and first non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
Given a proper class $A$, a cardinal $\kappa$ is  \emph{$A$-super Reinhardt} if for every $\lambda>\kappa$, there is a Reinhardt embedding ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{V}$ satisfying $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\kappa$, $j(\kappa)>\lambda$ and $j^+(A)=A$, where $$j^+(A) ~ = ~ \bigcup_{\alpha\in\operatorname{Ord}} j(A\cap V_\alpha).$$ 
  
A cardinal is  \emph{super Reinhardt} if it is $V$-super Reinhardt.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
A cardinal $\kappa$ is  \emph{totally Reinhardt} if $$\langle V_\kappa,V_{\kappa+1},\in\rangle\models \textnormal{ZF}_2  +  \textit{``There exists an $A$-super Reinhardt cardinal"}$$ holds for every  $A\in V_{\kappa+1}\setminus A$.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lemma:SuperReinhardtExacting}
    If $\delta$ is a super Reinhardt cardinal, then $\delta$ is a limit of  rank-Berkeley cardinals $\zeta<\delta$ that are limits of rank-Berkeley cardinals $\lambda$ with $V_\lambda\prec V_\delta$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Fix $\alpha<\delta$ and pick an elementary embedding  ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{V}$ with critical point $\delta$. Let $\eta$ denote the first non-trivial fixed point  of $j$. Since $V_\delta\prec V$, it follows that $\eta$ is a rank-Berkeley cardinal with $V_\eta\prec V$. Then there exists an elementary embedding ${i}:{V}\longrightarrow{V}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(i)=\delta$ and $i(\delta)>\eta$. We now have $V_\eta\prec V_{i(\delta)}$. It follows that $\delta$ is a limit of rank-Berkeley cardinals $\lambda$ with $V_\lambda\prec V_\delta$. The elementarity of $j$ then ensures that $\eta$ is a limit of rank-Berkeley cardinals $\lambda$ with $V_\lambda\prec V_\eta$. Since $V_\eta\prec V_{i(\delta)}$, we can now use the elementarity of $i$ to find a rank-Berkeley cardinal $\alpha<\zeta<\delta$ that is a limit of rank-Berkeley cardinals $\lambda$ with $V_\lambda\prec V_\delta$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{def:Magidorproduct2}\hfill
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item Given $E\subseteq D$, a condition in the \emph{Magidor product}
     $${\mathbb{P}}_E ~ = ~ \prod^{\mathrm{Mag}}_{\delta\in E}{\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}_\delta}$$
     of the sequence $\langle{{\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}_\delta}}~\vert~{\delta\in E}\rangle$ is a sequence
     $\langle{p_\delta}~\vert~{\delta\in E}\rangle$ with the property that $p_\delta$ is a
     condition in ${\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}_\delta}$ for all $\delta\in E$ and the stem of
     $p_\delta$ is empty for all but finitely-many $\delta\in E$.
 
 
     \item Given conditions $\vec{p}=\langle{p_\delta}~\vert~{\delta\in E}\rangle$ and
     $\vec{q}=\langle{q_\delta}~\vert~{\delta\in E}\rangle$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_E$, we define
     $\vec{p}\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_E}\vec{q}$ to hold if
     $p_\delta\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}_\delta}}q_\delta$ holds for all $\delta\in E$ and
     $p_\delta\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}_\delta}}^*q_\delta$ holds for all but finitely-many
     $\delta\in E$.
      
     In addition, we define $\vec{p}\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_E}^*\vec{q}$ to hold if
     $p_\delta\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}_\delta}}^*q_\delta$ holds for all $\delta\in E$.
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{MagProdProps}
The following statements hold for all $\delta\in D$:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item\label{MagProdProp21} The partial order ${\mathbb{P}}_D$ is isomorphic to
  $$
    {\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}\times{\mathbb{P}}_\delta\times{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)},
  $$
  and ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ is isomorphic to
  ${\mathbb{P}}_\delta\times{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)}$. Both isomorphisms also
  preserve the direct extension orders.
 
  \item\label{MagProdProp22} In every ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}$-generic extension
  $V[G]$ of the ground model $V$, the partial order ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$
  is weakly homogeneous, $\langle{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta},
  \leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}},\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}}^*\rangle$ is
  of Prikry-type and $\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}}^*$ is
  ${<}\delta$-directed-closed.
 
  \item\label{MagProdProp23} In every ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}$-generic extension
  $V[G]$ of the ground model $V$, forcing with ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ adds
  no new subsets of ordinals less than $\delta$. In particular, if $\xi$ is an
  ordinal with $|V_\xi|<\delta$, then $V_\xi$ is computed the same way in
  $V[G]$ and in every ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$-generic extension of $V[G]$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
\eqref{MagProdProp21} The natural decomposition map serves as an isomorphism
in both cases: splitting a condition according to the given partition of $D$
preserves both $\leq$ and $\leq^*$, and the requirement that only finitely
many coordinates carry a non-empty stem is equivalent to the conjunction of
the corresponding requirements for the factors.
 
\smallskip
 
\eqref{MagProdProp22} Set $\sigma=\sup(D\cap\delta)$, so that $\sigma<\delta$
because $D$ is discrete. Two conditions of ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}$ with the same
stems are compatible, and the number of possible sequences of stems is at most
$\sigma$. Consequently, ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}$ satisfies the $\sigma^+$-chain
condition in $V$. Moreover $|{\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}|\leq 2^\sigma<\delta$, because
$\delta$ is inaccessible. Let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}$-generic over $V$.
 
Since ${\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}_\eta}$ is weakly homogeneous in $V$ for every $\eta\in D$, and weak
homogeneity is preserved by Magidor products, the partial order
${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ is weakly homogeneous in $V$. As the isomorphisms
witnessing this are elements of $V$ and compatibility of conditions is
absolute, it follows that ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ is also weakly homogeneous
in $V[G]$.
 
Next, since $|{\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}|<\delta\leq\eta$ for every
$\eta\in D\setminus\delta$, the Levy--Solovay theorem implies that
$$
  \bar{{\mathcal{U}}}_\eta ~ = ~
  \{{X\in\mathcal{P}^{V[G]}(\eta)}~\vert~{\exists A\in{\mathcal{U}}_\eta ~ A\subseteq X}\}
$$
is a normal ultrafilter on $\eta$ in $V[G]$. Working in $V[G]$, define
$$
  {\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta} ~ = ~
  \prod_{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}^{\mathrm{Mag}}{\mathbb{P}}_{\bar{{\mathcal{U}}}_\eta}.
$$
Results of Magidor in \cite{HowlargeMagidor} then show that
$\langle{\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta},\leq_{{\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}},
\leq^*_{{\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}}\rangle$ is of Prikry-type in $V[G]$.
Moreover, the ordering $\leq^*_{{\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}}$ is ${<}\delta$-directed-closed
in $V[G]$: the members of a directed family all have the same stems,
and, since each $\bar{{\mathcal{U}}}_\eta$ is ${<}\eta$-complete in $V[G]$ and
$\delta\leq\eta$, fewer than $\delta$-many of the corresponding measure one
sets can be intersected coordinatewise.
 
Both properties are inherited by $\leq^*$-dense subposets. Indeed, assume that
${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ is a $\leq^*$-dense subposet of
${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$, {i.e.,}\ that every condition of
${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$ has a $\leq^*$-stronger condition in
${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$. Since $\leq^*$ refines $\leq$, the partial order
${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ is then also dense in ${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$,
so both partial orders have the same generic extensions and the same forcing
relation. Given a statement $\varphi$ of the forcing language and a condition
$\vec{p}$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$, the Prikry property of
${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$ provides $\vec{p}^{\,*}\leq^*\vec{p}$ in
${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$ deciding $\varphi$, and $\leq^*$-density yields
$\vec{q}\leq^*\vec{p}^{\,*}$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$, which then also
decides $\varphi$. Similarly, a $\leq^*$-directed family of size less than
$\delta$ in ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ has a $\leq^*$-lower bound in
${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$, and any condition of ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$
that is $\leq^*$-stronger than this bound is a $\leq^*$-lower bound of the
family in ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$.
 
It therefore suffices to show that ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ is a
$\leq^*$-dense subposet of ${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$. Let
$\vec{p}=\langle{p_\eta}~\vert~{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}\rangle$ be a condition in
${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$ and, given $\eta\in D\setminus\delta$, let
$s_\eta$ denote the stem of $p_\eta$ and let $A_\eta\in\bar{{\mathcal{U}}}_\eta$
denote the second component of $p_\eta$. By the definition of
$\bar{{\mathcal{U}}}_\eta$, working in $V[G]$ we may pick a sequence
$\langle{B_\eta\in{\mathcal{U}}_\eta}~\vert~{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}\rangle$ with the property that
$B_\eta\subseteq A_\eta$ holds for all $\eta\in D\setminus\delta$.
 
Fix a ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}$-name $\dot{B}$ for the sequence
$\langle{B_\eta}~\vert~{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}\rangle$ and, in $V$, set
$$
  {\mathcal{C}}_\eta ~ = ~
  \{{C\in{\mathcal{U}}_\eta}~\vert~{\exists p\in{\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta} ~
  p\Vdash\dot{B}(\check{\eta})=\check{C}}\}.
$$
Conditions forcing distinct values of $\dot{B}(\check\eta)$ are incompatible,
so the $\sigma^+$-chain condition ensures that $|{\mathcal{C}}_\eta|\leq\sigma$ holds
for all $\eta\in D\setminus\delta$; hence the sequence
$\langle{{\mathcal{C}}_\eta\in[{\mathcal{U}}_\eta]^{\leq\sigma}}~\vert~{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}\rangle$
belongs to $V$ and $B_\eta\in{\mathcal{C}}_\eta$ for all $\eta\in D\setminus\delta$.
 
By the definition of the Magidor product, the set
$\{{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}~\vert~{s_\eta\neq\emptyset}\}$ is finite, and each
$s_\eta$ is a finite sequence of ordinals; in particular, it follows that the
sequence $\langle{s_\eta}~\vert~{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}\rangle$ is an element of $V$. We
then know that $V$ contains the sequence
$\vec{q}=\langle{q_\eta}~\vert~{\eta\in D\setminus\delta}\rangle$ with the property that
$$
  q_\eta ~ = ~ \bigl\langle s_\eta,\textstyle\bigcap{\mathcal{C}}_\eta\bigr\rangle
$$
holds for all $\eta\in D\setminus\delta$. Since ${\mathcal{U}}_\eta$ is
${<}\eta$-complete in $V$ and $|{\mathcal{C}}_\eta|\leq\sigma<\delta\leq\eta$, we have
$\bigcap{\mathcal{C}}_\eta\in{\mathcal{U}}_\eta$; after removing from $\bigcap{\mathcal{C}}_\eta$ its
finitely many elements below $\max(s_\eta)$, which affects only the finitely
many coordinates with $s_\eta\neq\emptyset$, it follows that $\vec{q}$ is a
condition in ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ in $V$ and hence also a condition in
${\mathbb{P}}^G_{D\setminus\delta}$ in $V[G]$. Finally, $B_\eta\in{\mathcal{C}}_\eta$ implies
$\bigcap{\mathcal{C}}_\eta\subseteq B_\eta\subseteq A_\eta$ for all
$\eta\in D\setminus\delta$, and $\vec{q}$ and $\vec{p}$ have the same stems.
Therefore $\vec{q}$ is $\leq^*$-stronger than $\vec{p}$ in $V[G]$.
 
\smallskip
 
\eqref{MagProdProp23} Let $\rho<\delta$, let $\vec{p}$ be a condition in
${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ and let $\dot{X}$ be a
${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$-name for a subset of $\rho$. Using
\eqref{MagProdProp22}, recursively construct a $\leq^*$-decreasing sequence
$\langle{\vec{p}_\alpha}~\vert~{\alpha\leq\rho}\rangle$ of conditions below $\vec{p}$ such that
$\vec{p}_{\alpha+1}$ decides the statement ``$\check{\alpha}\in\dot{X}$'',
using the Prikry property at successor steps and the
${<}\delta$-directed-closure of $\leq^*$ at limit steps. Then $\vec{p}_\rho$
decides all statements ``$\check{\alpha}\in\dot{X}$'' with $\alpha<\rho$ and
therefore forces $\dot{X}$ to be equal to a set in $V[G]$. The second
assertion follows by induction on $\xi$, coding the elements of $V_\xi$ by
subsets of $|V_\xi|<\delta$.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{corollary:MagidorSupportPreserveInaccessible}
   Let $\nu=\sup(D)$ and assume that $\nu$ is an
   inaccessible cardinal. Then forcing with ${\mathbb{P}}_D$ preserves the
   inaccessibility of $\nu$.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Let $G$ be ${\mathbb{P}}_D$-generic over $V$ and let $\rho<\nu$. Fix $\delta\in D$
  with $\rho<\delta$ and let $G_{{<}\delta}\times G_{{\geq}\delta}$ denote the
  filter on ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}\times{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta}$ induced by $G$
  through Lemma~\ref{MagProdProps}.\eqref{MagProdProp21}. By
  Lemma~\ref{MagProdProps}.\eqref{MagProdProp23}, we have
  $\mathcal{P}(\rho)^{V[G]}=\mathcal{P}(\rho)^{V[G_{{<}\delta}]}$ and, since
  $|{\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}|<\delta<\nu$ and $\nu$ is inaccessible in $V$, this set
  has size less than $\nu$. Hence $\nu$ is a strong limit cardinal in $V[G]$.
 
 
  The regularity of $\nu$ in $V[G]$ follows similarly.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\begin{enumerate}
        \item $\langle \mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}},\leq,\leq^*\rangle$ is a Prikry-type forcing. 
        
        \item $\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}}$ preserves cardinals $\leq \kappa$.
        \item $\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}}$ forces $``{{\rm{cof}}(\kappa)}=\omega$".
        \item Forcing with $\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}}$ collapses all cardinals $\theta\in (\kappa,\mu]$, where $\mu=\lambda$ whenever ${{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}\geq \kappa$ and $\mu=\lambda^+$ whenever ${{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}<\kappa$. \qed
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lemma:BelowKappa}
  If $A$ denotes the set of all cardinals $\rho<\kappa$ with the property that
  there exists a normal ultrafilter ${\mathcal{F}}$ on $\rho$ such that $\rho$ is an
  exacting cardinal in $V_\lambda[H]$ whenever $H$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{\mathcal{F}}$-generic
  over $V_\lambda$, then $A\in{\mathcal{U}}$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Let $H$ be ${\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}}$-generic over $V_\lambda$. Every dense subset of
 ${\mathbb{P}}_{\mathcal{U}}$ in $V$ has rank less than $\lambda$ and is therefore an element
 of $V_\lambda$, so $H$ is also ${\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}}$-generic over $V$ and
 Corollary \ref{corollary:ExactingModels}.\eqref{item:ExactingModels2}  shows that $\kappa$ is an exacting cardinal in
 $V[H]$. Since ${\mathbb{P}}_{\mathcal{U}}$ is an element of $V_\lambda$, we have
 $V[H]_\lambda=V_\lambda[H]$, and this is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$ because
 $V_{\kappa_n}$ is an elementary submodel of $V_\lambda$ for all $n<\omega$.
 Proposition~\ref{prop:ExactingRankSegments} therefore shows that $\kappa$ is also
 an exacting cardinal in $V_\lambda[H]$.
  
 Since $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $V_\lambda\subseteq M$ imply
 $j(V_\lambda)=V_\lambda$, the set $j(A)$ is the set of all cardinals
 $\rho<\kappa_1$ for which there exists a normal ultrafilter ${\mathcal{F}}$ on $\rho$
 in $M$ such that $\rho$ is an exacting cardinal in $V_\lambda[H]$ whenever
 $H$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{\mathcal{F}}$-generic over $V_\lambda$. As ${\mathcal{U}}$ is an element of
 $V_\lambda\subseteq M$ and all of the above computations take place in
 $V_\lambda$ and in its generic extensions, and are therefore performed the
 same way in $V$ and in $M$, these observations show that $\kappa$ is an
 element of $j(A)$ and this means that $A$ is an element of ${\mathcal{U}}$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lemma:ManyExacting}
  Assume that  $V_\lambda$ is a model of $V=\textnormal{gHOD}$.\footnote{Recall that, by Lemma~\ref{lemma:I2andVHOD}, this assumption is compatible with the existence of an I2-cardinal.}
  If $G$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_D$-generic over $V$ and $\delta\in D$, then $\delta$ is an
  exacting cardinal in $V_\lambda[G]$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Fix $\delta\in D$ and let $\delta_*=\min(D\setminus(\delta+1))$ denote the
  least element of $D$ above $\delta$. Since $\delta_*$ is inaccessible and
  greater than $\delta$, we have $|V_{\delta+\omega}|<\delta_*$.
   
  Let $G_{{<}\delta}\times g\times G_{{>}\delta}$ be the filter on
  ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}\times{\mathbb{P}}_\delta\times{\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)}$
  induced by $G$ through the isomorphism provided by
  Lemma~\ref{MagProdProps}.\eqref{MagProdProp21} and set
  $W=V_\lambda[G_{{<}\delta}\times g]$, so that $V_\lambda[G]$ is a
  ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)}$-generic extension of $W$.
   
  Our
  setup new ensures that $\delta$ is an exacting cardinal in $V_\lambda[g]$.
   
  Moreover, since $D$ is discrete, it follows that the partial order
  ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta}$ is an element of $H(\delta)^{V_\lambda[g]}$ and we can
  use Lemma~\ref{lemma:ExactingSmallForcing} in $V_\lambda[g]$ to conclude
  that $\delta$ is exacting in $W$.
 
  Assume, towards a contradiction, that $\delta$ is not an exacting cardinal in
  $V_\lambda[G]$. By Lemma \ref{fact:CharExacting}, this means that, in
  $V_\lambda[G]$, there exists a non-empty ordinal definable subset $B$ of
  $V_{\delta+1}$ with the property that for all $x,y\in B$, there is no
  non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\delta,\in,x\rangle$ into
  $\langle V_\delta,\in,y\rangle$.
   
  Since ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)}={\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus\delta_*}$ and
  $G_{{<}\delta}\times g$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\cap\delta_*}$-generic over $V$,
  Lemma~\ref{MagProdProps}.\eqref{MagProdProp23} applied at $\delta_*$ shows
  that forcing with ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)}$ over $W$ does not add new
  elements of $V_{\delta+\omega}$. In particular, we have
  $V_{\delta+1}^{V_\lambda[G]}=V_{\delta+1}^{W}$ and $B\in W$.
   
  Since $V_\lambda$ is a model of "$V=\textnormal{gHOD}$", we now know that
  ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)}$ is an element of $\textnormal{HOD}^{W}$. Moreover, the fact
  that Lemma~\ref{MagProdProps}.\eqref{MagProdProp22} ensures that
  ${\mathbb{P}}_{D\setminus(\delta+1)}$ is weakly homogeneous in $W$ allows us to
  conclude that $\textnormal{OD}^{V_\lambda[G]}\cap W$ is contained in $\textnormal{OD}^{W}$ and hence
  that $B$ is a non-empty ordinal definable subset of $V_{\delta+1}$ in $W$.
   
  Since $\delta$ is an exacting cardinal in $W$, we can use
   Lemma \ref{fact:CharExacting} to find $x,y\in B$ and a non-trivial elementary
  embedding of $\langle V_\delta,\in,x\rangle$ into
  $\langle V_\delta,\in,y\rangle$ in $W$. But, since $W\subseteq V_\lambda[G]$,
  this embedding is also a non-trivial elementary embedding of
  $\langle V_\delta,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\delta,\in,y\rangle$ in
  $V_\lambda[G]$, contradicting our choice of $B$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Assume that $V$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$ containing an I2-embedding.
   
  Then there exists a class forcing extension $N$ of $V$ which is a model of
  $$\textnormal{ZFC} ~ + ~ \textit{``}V=\textnormal{gHOD}\textit{''} ~ + ~
  \textit{``There is an I2-embedding''}$$
  and in which, moreover, $V_\lambda$ is a model of $V=\textnormal{gHOD}$ for the first
  non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$ of that embedding.
   
  Work in $N$, let $\kappa<\lambda$, $D$ and ${\mathbb{P}}_D$ be as above and let $G$
  be ${\mathbb{P}}_D$-generic over $N$.
   
  By Lemma \ref{lemma:ManyExacting}, every $\delta\in D$ is an exacting
  cardinal in $N[G]_\lambda$, and $D$ is unbounded in $\kappa$. Since
  $\kappa=\sup(D)$ is inaccessible in $N$, Corollary
  \ref{corollary:MagidorSupportPreserveInaccessible} shows that $\kappa$ is
  inaccessible in $N[G]$ and therefore $N[G]_\kappa$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$. By
  Proposition~\ref{prop:ExactingRankSegments}, every $\delta\in D$ is then an
  exacting cardinal in $N[G]_\kappa$.
   
  Consequently, $N[G]_\kappa$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$ in which unboundedly many
  ordinals are exacting cardinals, {i.e.,} a set-sized model of the theory
  $$\textnormal{ZFC} ~ + ~ \textit{``There is a proper class of exacting cardinals''}.$$
  By the L\"owenheim--Skolem theorem and Mostowski collapsing, it
  follows that $N[G]$ contains a countable transitive model of this theory.
  Since the existence of such a model can be expressed by a
  $\Sigma^1_2$-sentence, \emph{Shoenfield absoluteness} ensures that such a
  model exists in $V$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
\eqref{item:ExactingLimit1} Assume that $\eta$ is an exacting limit of exacting cardinals. Since $\textnormal{HOD}^{V_\eta}$ is a subset of $\textnormal{HOD}$ and exacting cardinals are regular in $\textnormal{HOD}$, it follows that, in $V_\eta$, there is a proper class of
    singular cardinals that are regular in $\textnormal{HOD}$. Since $\eta$ is exacting,  there is an I3-embedding ${i}:{V_\eta}\longrightarrow{V_\eta}$ and therefore, in    $V_\eta$, there is an extendible cardinal below a huge cardinal. By
    Woodin's HOD Dichotomy (Theorem \ref{thm:HODdichotomy}), this contradicts the Weak HOD Conjecture. 

   \eqref{item:ExactingLimit2} Assume, towards a contradiction, that there is a limit cardinal $\kappa$ of uncountable cofinality with the property that the set $E$ of exacting
    cardinals below $\kappa$ is stationary in $\kappa$. Then $E$ intersects    the set of all limit points of $E$ in $\kappa$ and hence there exists an exacting limit of exacting cardinals. This contradicts \eqref{item:ExactingLimit1}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lemma:WoodinForcingExacting}
  If $\lambda$ is a rank-Berkeley cardinal and $\delta>\lambda$ is a supercompact cardinal with $V_\lambda\prec {V_\delta}$, then ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{{\mathbb{Q}}_\delta}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }"$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Assume, towards a contradiction, that the statement of the lemma fails.     We may then assume that $\delta$ is the minimal supercompact cardinal above $\lambda$ satisfying $V_\lambda\prec {V_\delta}$ for which the given conclusion fails. Since the partial order ${\mathbb{Q}}_\delta$ is weakly homogeneous and definable in $V_\delta$ by a formula without parameters, our assumption ensures that the cardinal $\delta$ is definable by a formula with parameter $\lambda$. The analysis of \cite{SEM1} now shows that ${\mathbb{Q}}_\delta$ is forcing equivalent to a two-step iteration ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda*\dot{{\mathbb{P}}}$ satisfying the following: 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The partial order ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda$ is definable in $V_{\lambda+1}$ by a formula without parameters and forcing with ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda$ preserves unboundedly many regular cardinals below $\lambda$. 

        \item\label{item:WoodinForcing2} Given a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{V_{\lambda+1}}\longrightarrow{V_{\lambda+1}}$ with first non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$,   there exists a condition $p_j$ in ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda$ with the property that $$G ~ = ~ \{{p\in{\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda}~\vert~{j(p)\in G}\}$$ holds whenever $G$ is ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda$-generic over $V$ with $p_j\in G$. 
                                                                                             

        \item\label{item:WoodinForcing3} If $G$ is ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda$-generic over $V$, then, in $V[G]$, the partial order $\dot{{\mathbb{P}}}^G$ is ${<}\lambda^+$-closed, weakly homogeneous and definable in $V_\delta$ without parameters. 

        \item\label{item:WoodinForcing4} If $G$ is ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda$-generic over $V$, then $\textsf{\textup{DC}}_\lambda$ holds in $V[G]$. 
    \end{enumerate}


  Pick $\zeta>\delta$ such that $V_\zeta$ is sufficiently elementary in $V$. Then there exists an elementary embedding ${j}:{V_\zeta}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ such that $\operatorname{crit}(j)<\lambda$ and $\lambda$ is the first non-trivial fixed point of $j$. We then have ${{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}=\omega$,  $j(\delta)=\delta$ and $j({\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda)={\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda$. Let $p_j$ be the condition given by \eqref{item:WoodinForcing2} and let $G*H$ be $({\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda*\dot{{\mathbb{P}}})$-generic over $V$ with $p_j\in G$. Then $V_\zeta[G]=V[G]_\zeta$, $\zeta\in(C^{(2)})^{V[G]}$ and $j[G]\subseteq G$. In particular, there is a canonical lifting $${j_G}:{V[G]_\zeta}\longrightarrow{V[G]_\zeta}$$ of $j$ to $V[G]_\zeta$. 
   
  We can now apply Theorem \ref{theorem:UltraexactingInnerModels} in $V[G]$ with $N=V[G]$ and $X_0=X_1=V[G]_\zeta$ to conclude that $\lambda$ is ultraexacting in $V[G]$. 

  Now, by \eqref{item:WoodinForcing3} and \eqref{item:WoodinForcing4}, forcing with $\dot{{\mathbb{P}}}^G$ over $V[G]$ does not add new subsets of $V_\lambda$. Moreover, \eqref{item:WoodinForcing3} ensures that the partial order $\dot{{\mathbb{P}}}^G$ is weakly homogeneous and ordinal definable in $V[G]$. This allows us to apply Lemma \ref{prop:PreserveExactingGoodForcing}.\eqref{prop:ZFforcingPreserve2} to conclude that $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $V[G,H]$. 

  These computations contradict our initial assumption,  because, in $V$,  the partial order ${\mathbb{Q}}_\delta$ is weakly homogeneous and forcing equivalent to ${\mathbb{Q}}_\lambda*\dot{{\mathbb{P}}}$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
If there exists a super Reinhardt cardinal, then there exists a set-sized transitive model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$  with  a proper class of ultraexacting cardinals that are limits of ultraexacting cardinals.
<!-- end cor-4 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Let $\delta$ be a super Reinhardt cardinal. Then $\delta$ is supercompact and therefore a combination of results in \cite{SEM1} with Proposition \ref{prop:ZFExactingDown}, Lemma \ref{lemma:SuperReinhardtExacting} and Lemma \ref{lemma:WoodinForcingExacting} shows that if $G$ is ${\mathbb{Q}}_\delta$-generic over $V$, then $V[G]_\delta$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$  with a proper class of ultraexacting cardinals that are limits of ultraexacting cardinals. In particular, there is a generic extension of the ground model $V$ that contains a countable transitive model of $\mathrm{ZFC}$ with a proper class of ultraexacting cardinals that are limits of ultraexacting cardinals. Shoenfield absoluteness then ensures that such a model already exists in $V$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lemma:StatUltra}
    If $\delta$ is a cardinal that is both supercompact and totally Reinhardt, $G$ is ${\mathbb{Q}}_\delta$-generic over $V$ and $H$ is $\mathop{\mathrm{Col}}({<}\delta,V_\delta)$-generic over $V[G]$, then, in $V[G,H]$,  every closed unbounded subset of $\delta$ contains an ultraexacting cardinal.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
The results of \cite{SEM1} show that, in $V$, the partial order ${\mathbb{Q}}_\delta$ is forcing equivalent to a two-step iteration ${\mathbb{Q}}*\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}$ such that ${\mathbb{Q}}$ is a partial order in $V_\delta$ that forces $\textsf{\textup{DC}}$ to hold and $\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}$ to be a $\sigma$-closed partial order that  is a subset of $V_\delta$. Let $G_0*G_1$ be $({\mathbb{Q}}*\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}})$-generic over $V$ with $V[G]=V[G_0,G_1]$. We then know that $\delta$ is supercompact and totally Reinhardt in $V[G_0]$. 
     
    Moreover, the results of \cite{SEM1}  show that every element of $V[G]_\delta$ has a $\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}^{G_0}$-name in $V[G_0]_\delta$. 
     
    Therefore, it follows that $V[G,H]$ is a forcing extension of $V[G_0]$ using a partial order ${\mathbb{C}}$ that is a subset of $V[G_0]_\delta$ and $\sigma$-closed in $V[G_0]$. 

    Fix a ${\mathbb{C}}$-name $\dot{C}\in V[G_0]$ for a closed unbounded subset of $\delta$ and a condition $p_*$ in ${\mathbb{C}}$. We can now find  $A\in V[G_0]_{\delta+1}$ coding the condition $p_*$, the ordering $\leq_{\mathbb{C}}$ of ${\mathbb{C}}$ and the subset $$D ~ = ~ \{{\langle p,\beta\rangle\in{\mathbb{C}}\times\delta}~\vert~{p\Vdash^{V[G_0]}_{\mathbb{C}}"\beta\in\dot{C}\hspace{0.8pt}"}\}$$ of $V_\delta$. Since $\delta$ is totally Reinhardt in $V[G_0]$, we can find $\kappa<\delta$ that is $A$-super Reinhardt in $\langle V[G_0]_\delta,V[G_0]_{\delta+1},\in\rangle$. Our setup then ensures that the condition $p_*$ is an element of ${\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_\kappa$. 


    Given $p\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_\kappa$ and $\alpha<\kappa$, there exists $\gamma_{\alpha,p}<\delta$ with the property that there exist $\alpha<\beta<\gamma_{\alpha,p}$ and  $q\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_{\gamma_{\alpha,p}}$ with $q\leq_{\mathbb{C}} p$ and $\langle q,\beta\rangle\in D$. Since $\delta$ is strongly inaccessible in $V[G_0]$, we can find $\rho<\delta$ with $\gamma_{\alpha,p}<\rho$ for all $p\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_\kappa$ and $\alpha<\kappa$. 
     
    Therefore, we can find a non-trivial elementary embedding ${j}:{V[G_0]_\delta}\longrightarrow{V[G_0]_\delta}$  with $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\kappa$, $j(\kappa)>\rho$ as well as $$j({\leq_{\mathbb{C}}}\cap V_\alpha) ~ = ~ {\leq_{\mathbb{C}}} \cap V_{j(\alpha)}$$ and  $$j(D  \cap  V_\alpha) ~ = ~ D  \cap  V_{j(\alpha)}$$ for all $\alpha<\kappa$. 
     
    The elementarity of $j$ then ensures that for every condition  $p\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_\kappa$ and every $\alpha<\kappa$, there exists a condition  $q\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_\kappa$ and $\alpha\leq\beta<\kappa$ with $q\leq_{\mathbb{C}} p$ and $\langle q,\beta\rangle\in D$. 
    
    Let $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j$ and set $\lambda=\sup_{n<\omega}\kappa_n$. Since $\delta$ is a regular cardinal in $V[G_0]$, we have $\lambda<\delta$.  
     
    Elementarity then ensures that for every $n<\omega$, every $p\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_{\kappa_n}$ and every $\alpha<\kappa_n$, there exist $q\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_{\kappa_n}$ and $\alpha\leq\beta<\kappa_n$ with the property that  $q\leq_{\mathbb{C}} p$ and $\langle q,\beta\rangle\in D$. This allows us to use $\textsf{\textup{DC}}$ in $V[G_0]$ to find a $\leq_{\mathbb{C}}$-descending sequence $\langle{p_n\in{\mathbb{C}}\cap V[G_0]_{\kappa_n}}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ with $p_0=p_*$ and the property that for all $n<\omega$, there exists $\kappa_n\leq\beta_n<\kappa_{n+1}$ with $\langle q_{n+1},\beta_n\rangle\in D$. Since ${\mathbb{C}}$ is $\sigma$-closed in $V[G_0]$, we can find a condition $p_\omega$ in ${\mathbb{C}}$ with $p_\omega\leq_{\mathbb{C}} p_n$ for all $n<\omega$. 
    
    Let $F$ be ${\mathbb{C}}$-generic over $V[G_0]$ with $p_\omega\in F$. Then $\dot{C}^F\cap[\kappa_n,\kappa_{n+1})\neq\emptyset$ holds for all $n<\omega$ and therefore we know that $\lambda$ is an element of $\dot{C}^F$. 
     
    Earlier arguments show that $\lambda$ is a rank-Berkeley cardinal in $V[G_0]_\delta$ and $V[G_0]_\lambda\prec V[G_0]_\delta$ holds. By Proposition \ref{prop:LocalRankBerkeleySupercompact}, this means that $\lambda$ is a rank-Berkeley cardinal in $V[G_0]$. Moreover, the analysis in \cite{SEM1} shows that $\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}^{G_0}={\mathbb{Q}}_\delta^{V[G_0]}$ holds, {i.e.,} $\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}^{G_0}$ satisfies the definition of Woodin's partial order in $V[G_0]$. 
     
    Let $F_0$ denote the filter on $\dot{{\mathbb{Q}}}^{G_0}$ induced by $F$. Then Lemma \ref{lemma:WoodinForcingExacting} shows that $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $V[G_0,F_0]$. Next, Proposition \ref{prop:PreserveExactingGoodForcing} ensures that $\lambda$ is ultraexacting in $V[G_0,F]$. 

    The above computations show that below every condition $p_*$ in ${\mathbb{C}}$, there exists a condition that forces $\dot{C}$ to contain an ultraexacting cardinal. A density argument now yields the statement of the lemma.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
If $\delta$ is a cardinal that is both supercompact and totally Reinhardt, $G$ is ${\mathbb{Q}}_\delta$-generic over $V$ and $H$ is $\mathop{\mathrm{Col}}({<}\delta,V_\delta)$-generic over $V[G]$, then $L(V[G]_\delta)[H]$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$ in which $\delta$ is a regular cardinal that is a stationary limit of ultraexacting cardinals.
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Since $\textsf{\textup{DC}}_{{<}\delta}$ holds in $V[G]$ and the partial order $\mathop{\mathrm{Col}}({<}\delta,V_\delta)$ is ${<}\delta$-closed in $V[G]$, we have    $V[G]_\delta=V[G,H]_\delta$ and the fact that $H$ codes a well-ordering of $V[G]_\delta$ ensures that $L(V[G]_\delta)[H]$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$. 
     
    Let $C$ be a closed unbounded subset of $\delta$ in $L(V[G]_\delta)[H]$. Then Lemma \ref{lemma:StatUltra} shows that $C$ contains an ordinal $\lambda$ that is an ultraexacting cardinal in $V[G,H]$. In this situation, the fact that $V[G]_\delta=V[G,H]_\delta$ allows us to use Proposition \ref{prop:ExactingDownToL} to see that $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $L(V[G]_\delta)$. 
     
    Finally, since $V[G]_\delta=V[G,H]_\delta$,     we can apply Proposition \ref{prop:PreserveExactingGoodForcing} in $L(V[G]_\delta)$ to conclude that $\lambda$ is also an ultraexacting cardinal in $L(V[G]_\delta)[H]$.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
In the following, assume that $\lambda$ is a limit of Woodin cardinals and ${\mathbb{P}}\in V_\lambda$ is a partial order that forces $\lambda$ to have countable cofinality. Fix a Woodin cardinal $\delta<\lambda$ with ${\mathbb{P}}\in V_\delta$ and  an inaccessible cardinal $\delta<\rho<\lambda$. 
     
    Let ${\mathbb{Q}}_{{<}\delta}$ denote Woodin's countable stationary tower forcing (see \cite{stationarytower} for details). 

   Now, let $g$ be ${\mathbb{Q}}_{<\delta}$-generic over $V$ and let    $${j_g}:{V}\longrightarrow{M_g\subseteq V[g]}$$ denote the generic elementary embedding induced by $g$. Standard stationary tower forcing arguments (see \cite{stationarytower}) then show that the following statements hold: 
   \begin{itemize}
       \item $\operatorname{crit}(j_g)=\omega_1^V$ and $j_g(\omega_1^V)=\delta$. 
       
       \item $M_g = \{{j_g(f)(\alpha)}~\vert~{{f}:{\omega_1^V}\longrightarrow{V}, ~ \alpha <\delta}\}$. 
       
       \item  $({}^\omega M_g)^{V[g]}\subseteq M_g$.
   \end{itemize}

   Since $\mathcal{P}({\mathbb{P}})^V$ is countable in $V[g]$, we can find a filter $G$ on ${\mathbb{P}}$ in $V[g]$ that is generic over $V$. 
   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
     
    In addition, results of Hamkins, Laver and Woodin (see \cite{MR2364192})  show that there is a parameter $p\in V_\rho$ with the property that the class $V$ is definable in $V[g]$ by a formula with parameter $p$. This directly implies that the class $M_g$ is definable in $V[g]$ from the parameters $g$ and $p$. 
     
    Finally, the construction of $M_g$ as an ultrapower ensures that all sufficiently large inaccessible cardinals below $\lambda$ are fixed points of $j_g$. Since the embedding $j_g$ is continuous at ordinal of countable cofinality in $V$, this directly yields the following statements: 


   \begin{claim*}
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\lambda$ has countable cofinality in $V$, then $j_g(\lambda)=\lambda$. 

        \item If $\lambda$ has uncountable cofinality in $V$ and $C$ is a closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ in $V$, then $\lambda\in j_g(C)$. \qed 
    \end{enumerate}
   \end{claim*}


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       

   \begin{claim*}
     If ${j}:{V[g]_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V[G]_\lambda}$ is an I3-embedding with $\operatorname{crit}(j)>\rho$ in $V[g]$, then the map $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is an element of $M_g$. 
   \end{claim*}

   \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
     Let $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j$. 
     
     Fix some $0<n<\omega$. Since ${\mathbb{Q}}_{{<}\delta}$ is an element of $V_{\kappa_0}$, we can apply {\cite[Lemma 4]{MR2364192}} to see that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_{\kappa_n}$ is an element of the ground model $V$ and we let $E$ denote the $(\kappa_0,\kappa_n)$-extender derived from this embedding in $V$. Then $E$ is $\rho$-complete in $V$ (as defined in {\cite[Definition 146]{SEM1}}). 
      
     Let ${i_E}:{V}\longrightarrow{M_E}$ denote the  ultrapower embedding given by $E$ in $V$. The definition of $E$ then ensures that $i_E\mathbin\upharpoonright V_{\kappa_{n-1}}=j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_{\kappa_{n-1}}$. Let $E^\prime$ denote the canonical $(\kappa_0,\kappa_n)$-extender induced by $E$ in $V[g]$ and let ${i_{E^\prime}}:{V[g]}\longrightarrow{M_{E^\prime}}$ denote the corresponding ultrapower embedding constructed in $V[g]$. Then $i_{E^\prime}$ is the canonical lifting of $i_E$ to the ${\mathbb{Q}}_{{<}\delta}$-generic extension and this directly implies that 
       \begin{equation}\label{equation:ExactingEmbeddingsCoincides}
           i_{E^\prime}\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_{\kappa_{n-1}} ~ = ~ j\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_{\kappa_{n-1}},
       \end{equation} because for each $z\in V[g]_{\kappa_{n-1}}$, there is a ${\mathbb{Q}}_{{<}\delta}$-name $\tau\in V_{\kappa_{n-1}}$ with $\tau^g=x$ and $$j(x) ~ = ~ j(\tau^g) ~ = ~ j(\tau)^g ~ = ~ i_E(\tau)^g ~ = ~ i_{E^\prime}(x).$$ 


     Set $F=j_g(E)$. Note that our setup ensures that $j_g(\kappa_\ell)=\kappa_\ell$ holds for all $\ell<\omega$ and therefore we know that $F$ is a $(\kappa_0,\kappa_n)$-extender in $M_g$. Let ${i_F}:{M_g}\longrightarrow{M_F}$ denote the corresponding ultrapower embedding constructed in $M_g$. Earlier observations now show that the extender $E$ and the embedding $j_g$ satisfy the assumptions of {\cite[Lemma 147]{SEM1}} and this result then shows that $i_{E^\prime}\mathbin\upharpoonright M_g  =  i_F$ holds. In combination with \eqref{equation:ExactingEmbeddingsCoincides}, this shows that $$j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\kappa_{n-1}} ~ = ~ i_F\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\kappa_{n-1}} ~ \in ~ M_g.$$

    The above computations show that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\kappa_n}$ is an element of $M_g$ for every $n<\omega$. Since $M_g$ is closed under countable sequences in $V[g]$, we can now conclude that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is also an element of $M_g$.  
   \end{proof}


   \begin{claim*}
       If $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $V[G]$, then $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $M_g$. 
   \end{claim*}

   \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
       Assume, towards a contradiction, that $\lambda$ is not an exacting cardinal in $M_g$. By Theorem \ref{fact:CharExacting}, this shows that, in $M_g$, there is a non-empty ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$ with the property that for all $x,y\in A$, there is no non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle V_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$. Let $A$ be the least such subset in $M_g$ with respect to the canonical well-ordering of ordinal definable sets in $M_g$. Then the set $\{A\}$ is definable in $M_g$ by a formula with parameter $\lambda$. In this situation, our earlier observations show that the set $\{A\}$ is definable in $V[g]$ by a formula with parameters $\lambda$, $g$ and $p$. 

       
       Since $V[g]$ is a forcing extension of $V[G]$ using a partial order of size less than $\rho$, our assumption allows us to use Lemma \ref{lemma:ExactingSmallForcing}.\eqref{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing1} to show that $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $V[g]$. 
        
       Pick   $\zeta>\lambda$ such that $V[g]_\zeta$ is sufficiently elementary in $V[g]$ and use the exactingness of $\lambda$ in $V[g]$ to  find  an elementary submodel $X$ of $V[g]_\zeta$ in $V[g]$ containing $V[g]_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}$  as well as   an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V[g]_\zeta}$ in $V[g]$ satisfying $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\rho=\operatorname{id}_\rho$, $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$ and $j(\lambda)=\lambda$. 
        
       The fact that $\lambda$, $g$ and $p$ are elements of $X$ that are fixed by $j$ then ensures that $A$ and $(M_g)_\lambda$ are  elements of $X$ that are fixed by $j$. 
        
       By elementarity, there exists an $x\in A\cap X$. Set $y=j(x)\in A$. Then $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is a non-trivial  elementary embedding of $\langle(M_g)_\lambda,\in,x\rangle$ into $\langle(M_g)_\lambda,\in,y\rangle$. 
        
       Since $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_\lambda$ is an I3-embedding with critical point greater than $\rho$ in $V[g]$, our previous claim shows that the map $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is an element of $M_g$, contradicting our choice of $A$. 
   \end{proof}


      \begin{claim*}
       If $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $V[G]$, then $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $M_g$. 
   \end{claim*}

   \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
       Assume, towards a contradiction, that $\lambda$ is not an ultraexacting cardinal in $M_g$.  Theorem \ref{fact:CharUltraexacting} then implies that, in $M_g$, there is an ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$ with the property that there is no non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle$ into itself. Let $A$ be the least such subset in $M_g$ with respect to the canonical well-ordering of ordinal definable sets in $M_g$. Since the set $\{A\}$ is again definable in $M_g$ by a formula with parameter $\lambda$, it follows that the set $\{A\}$ is definable in $V[g]$ by a formula with parameters $\lambda$, $g$ and $p$. 

      Next, we apply Lemma \ref{lemma:ExactingSmallForcing}.\eqref{item:ExactingUltraSmallForcing2} to see that $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $V[g]$. 
       Fix  $\zeta>\lambda$ with the property that $V[g]$ is sufficiently elementary in $V[g]$,  an elementary submodel $X$ of $V[g]_\zeta$ in $V[g]$ containing $V[g]_\lambda$  and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V[g]_\zeta}$ in $V[g]$ satisfying $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\rho=\operatorname{id}_\rho$, $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$, $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_\lambda\in X$. 
        
       Then $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_\lambda$ is an I3-embedding in $V[g]$ and an earlier claim shows that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is an element of $M_g$. Define $${j_* ~ = ~ (j\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_\lambda)_+^{V[g]}}:{V[g]_{\lambda+1}}\longrightarrow{V[g]_{\lambda+1}}$$ (see \S\ref{subsection:RankIntoRank}). An application of  {\cite[Lemma 3.7]{ABL}} then shows that $j_*$ is an I1-embedding that is an element of $X$ and satisfies  $$j\mathbin\upharpoonright(V[g]_{\lambda+1}\cap X) ~ = ~ j_*\mathbin\upharpoonright(V[g]_{\lambda+1}\cap X).$$
        
       Since our setup ensures that $A$ and $(M_g)_{\lambda+1}$ are elements of $X$ that are fixed by $j$, it follows that, in $X$, the map $j_*\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\lambda+1}$ is an elementary embedding of $\langle(M_g)_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle$ into itself. The correctness properties of $X$ then ensure that $j_*\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\lambda+1}$ has the same property in $V[g]$. 
       
       
       Finally, the fact that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is an I3-embedding in $M_g$, allows us to define $${i ~ = ~ (j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda)_+^{M_g}}:{(M_g)_{\lambda+1}}\longrightarrow{(M_g)_{\lambda+1}}.$$ 
        
       Since $i\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda=j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda=j_*\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$,  it follows that $$j_*\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\lambda+1} ~ = ~ i ~ \in ~ M_g$$ and therefore we can conclude that $M_g$ contains a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle(M_g)_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle$ into itself, contradicting our choice of $A$. 
   \end{proof}


  We are now ready to prove the two parts of the theorem: 


  \eqref{item:LevySolovayBeyondHOD1} Assume that $\lambda$ is a cardinal with the property that $$\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}``\textit{$\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal }"$$ holds for some partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in V_\lambda$. 
   
  Since exacting cardinals are limits of Woodin cardinals,  {\cite[Corollary 25]{MR2063629}} shows that $\lambda$ is a limit of Woodin cardinals in $V$. In particular, our assumption allows us to  carry out the above constructions and conclude that $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in the model $M_g$. 
   
  If $\lambda$ has countable cofinality in $V$, then an earlier claim shows that $j_g(\lambda)=\lambda$ and the elementarity of $j_g$ implies that $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $V$. Moreover, if $\lambda$ has uncountable cofinality and $C$ is a closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ in $V$, then an earlier claim shows that $\lambda$ is an element of $j_g(C)$ and we can conclude that $C$ contains an exacting cardinal in $V$. 


  \eqref{item:LevySolovayBeyondHOD2} Assume that $\lambda$ is a cardinal with the property that $$\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}``\textit{$\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }"$$ holds for some partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in V_\lambda$. 
     
    As above, this assumption allows us to carry out the above constructions and conclude that $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in the model $M_g$. In addition, we can again conlcude that, if $\lambda$ has countable cofinality in $V$, then $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in $V$, and, if $\lambda$ has uncountable cofinality in $V$, then every closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ in $V$ contains a cardinal that is ultraexacting in $V$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- claim--4: body_md -->
\begin{enumerate}
        \item If $\lambda$ has countable cofinality in $V$, then $j_g(\lambda)=\lambda$. 

        \item If $\lambda$ has uncountable cofinality in $V$ and $C$ is a closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ in $V$, then $\lambda\in j_g(C)$. \qed 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end claim--4 -->
<!-- claim--5: body_md -->
If ${j}:{V[g]_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V[G]_\lambda}$ is an I3-embedding with $\operatorname{crit}(j)>\rho$ in $V[g]$, then the map $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is an element of $M_g$.
<!-- end claim--5 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Let $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j$. 
     
     Fix some $0<n<\omega$. Since ${\mathbb{Q}}_{{<}\delta}$ is an element of $V_{\kappa_0}$, we can apply {\cite[Lemma 4]{MR2364192}} to see that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_{\kappa_n}$ is an element of the ground model $V$ and we let $E$ denote the $(\kappa_0,\kappa_n)$-extender derived from this embedding in $V$. Then $E$ is $\rho$-complete in $V$ (as defined in {\cite[Definition 146]{SEM1}}). 
      
     Let ${i_E}:{V}\longrightarrow{M_E}$ denote the  ultrapower embedding given by $E$ in $V$. The definition of $E$ then ensures that $i_E\mathbin\upharpoonright V_{\kappa_{n-1}}=j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_{\kappa_{n-1}}$. Let $E^\prime$ denote the canonical $(\kappa_0,\kappa_n)$-extender induced by $E$ in $V[g]$ and let ${i_{E^\prime}}:{V[g]}\longrightarrow{M_{E^\prime}}$ denote the corresponding ultrapower embedding constructed in $V[g]$. Then $i_{E^\prime}$ is the canonical lifting of $i_E$ to the ${\mathbb{Q}}_{{<}\delta}$-generic extension and this directly implies that 
       \begin{equation}\label{equation:ExactingEmbeddingsCoincides}
           i_{E^\prime}\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_{\kappa_{n-1}} ~ = ~ j\mathbin\upharpoonright V[g]_{\kappa_{n-1}},
       \end{equation} because for each $z\in V[g]_{\kappa_{n-1}}$, there is a ${\mathbb{Q}}_{{<}\delta}$-name $\tau\in V_{\kappa_{n-1}}$ with $\tau^g=x$ and $$j(x) ~ = ~ j(\tau^g) ~ = ~ j(\tau)^g ~ = ~ i_E(\tau)^g ~ = ~ i_{E^\prime}(x).$$ 


     Set $F=j_g(E)$. Note that our setup ensures that $j_g(\kappa_\ell)=\kappa_\ell$ holds for all $\ell<\omega$ and therefore we know that $F$ is a $(\kappa_0,\kappa_n)$-extender in $M_g$. Let ${i_F}:{M_g}\longrightarrow{M_F}$ denote the corresponding ultrapower embedding constructed in $M_g$. Earlier observations now show that the extender $E$ and the embedding $j_g$ satisfy the assumptions of {\cite[Lemma 147]{SEM1}} and this result then shows that $i_{E^\prime}\mathbin\upharpoonright M_g  =  i_F$ holds. In combination with \eqref{equation:ExactingEmbeddingsCoincides}, this shows that $$j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\kappa_{n-1}} ~ = ~ i_F\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\kappa_{n-1}} ~ \in ~ M_g.$$

    The above computations show that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\kappa_n}$ is an element of $M_g$ for every $n<\omega$. Since $M_g$ is closed under countable sequences in $V[g]$, we can now conclude that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_\lambda$ is also an element of $M_g$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->

Theorem \ref{fact:CharUltraexacting} then implies that, in $M_g$, there is an ordinal definable subset $A$ of $V_{\lambda+1}$ with the property that there is no non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_{\lambda+1},\in,A\rangle$ into itself. An application of  {\cite[Lemma 3.7]{ABL}} then shows that $j_*$ is an I1-embedding that is an element of $X$ and satisfies  $$j\mathbin\upharpoonright(V[g]_{\lambda+1}\cap X) ~ = ~ j_*\mathbin\upharpoonright(V[g]_{\lambda+1}\cap X).$$

The correctness properties of $X$ then ensure that $j_*\mathbin\upharpoonright(M_g)_{\lambda+1}$ has the same property in $V[g]$.
