<!-- cor-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:LevySolovayCountableCof}
 Let $\lambda$ be a cardinal of countable cofinality. 
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item The following statements are equivalent: 
        \begin{enumerate}
      \item $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal. 

      \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal }"$ holds for every partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$.  
      
      \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal }"$ holds for some partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$.
  \end{enumerate}

       \item The following statements are equivalent: 
        \begin{enumerate}
      \item $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal. 

      \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }"$ holds for every partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$.  
      
      \item ${\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal }"$ holds for some partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$. \qed
  \end{enumerate}
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-5 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Assume that the weak HOD Conjecture is true. By Theorem \ref{theorem:ExactingLimit}, we then know that exacting cardinals are not limits of exacting cardinals. An application of Theorem \ref{theorem:LevySolovayBeyondHOD} then shows that no cardinal $\lambda$ of uncountable cofinality is forced to be exacting by a partial order in $H(\lambda)$. In particular, since exacting cardinals have countable cofinality and ultraexacting cardinals are exacting, the equivalences stated in the theorem directly follow from the ones provided by Corollary \ref{cor:LevySolovayCountableCof}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- cor-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:LevySolovayAbove}
 Let $\kappa$ be a cardinal. 
 \begin{enumerate}
     \item The following statements are equivalent: 
      \begin{enumerate}
          \item There is an exacting cardinal greater than $\kappa$. 

          \item There is a partial order of cardinality at most $\kappa$ that forces a cardinal greater than $\kappa$ to be exacting. 
      \end{enumerate}

     \item The following statements are equivalent: 
      \begin{enumerate}
          \item There is an ultraexacting cardinal greater than $\kappa$. 

          \item There is a partial order of cardinality at most $\kappa$ that forces a cardinal greater than $\kappa$ to be ultraexacting. \qed
      \end{enumerate} 
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end cor-6 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:Subtle}
    Exacting cardinals are subtle in $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Assume, towards a contradicting that there is an exacting cardinal $\lambda$ that is not subtle in $\textnormal{HOD}$. Let $\langle C,\vec{E}\rangle$ be the least pair in the canonical well-ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}$ with the property that $C$ is a closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ and $\vec{E}=\langle{E_\alpha}~\vert~{\alpha<\lambda}\rangle$ is a sequence with $E_\alpha\subseteq\alpha$ for all $\alpha<\lambda$ and $E_\alpha\neq E_\beta\cap\alpha$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in C$ with $\alpha<\beta$. Since the class of all proper initial segments of the canonical well-ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}$ is definable by a $\Sigma_2$-formula without parameters, it follows that the sets $\{C\}$ and $\{\vec{E}\}$ are definable by a $\Sigma_3$-formula with parameter $\lambda$. 

    Pick $\lambda<\zeta\in C^{(3)}$. Our assumptions now yield an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\zeta$ with $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ with $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$. We then know that $C,\vec{E}\in X$ with $j(C)=C$ and $j(\vec{E})=\vec{E}$. Let $\kappa$ denote the minimal ordinal below $\lambda$ with $j(\kappa)>\kappa$. 


    \begin{claim*}
       $\kappa\in C$. 
    \end{claim*}

    \begin{proof}[Proof of the Claim]
      Assume, towards a contradiction, that $\kappa$ is not an element of $C$ and set $\alpha=\min(C\setminus\kappa)>\kappa$. We then know that the set $\{\alpha\}$ is definable by a $\Sigma_3$-formula with parameters in $\kappa\cup\{\lambda\}$ and hence it follows that $j(\alpha)=\alpha$. But, this contradicts the fact that ${j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda}:{V_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}$ is an elementary embedding and hence, by Kunen's Theorem, no ordinal in the interval $(\kappa,\lambda)$ is fixed by $j$. 
    \end{proof}

    Elementarity now ensures that $j(\kappa)>\kappa$ is also an element of $C$ and $j(E_\kappa)=E_{j(\kappa)}$ holds. Since our setup  implies that $E_{j(\kappa)}\cap\kappa=j(E_\kappa)\cap\kappa=E_\kappa$, we have derived a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- claim--8: body_md -->
$\kappa\in C$.
<!-- end claim--8 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Assume, towards a contradiction, that $\kappa$ is not an element of $C$ and set $\alpha=\min(C\setminus\kappa)>\kappa$. We then know that the set $\{\alpha\}$ is definable by a $\Sigma_3$-formula with parameters in $\kappa\cup\{\lambda\}$ and hence it follows that $j(\alpha)=\alpha$. But, this contradicts the fact that ${j\mathbin\upharpoonright V_\lambda}:{V_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}$ is an elementary embedding and hence, by Kunen's Theorem, no ordinal in the interval $(\kappa,\lambda)$ is fixed by $j$.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{theorem:ExactingInHOD}
  Let  $\lambda$ be an exacting cardinal with the property that unboundedly many regular cardinals below $\lambda$ are not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$. 
    
  Then, in $\textnormal{HOD}$, for every $A\in V_{\lambda+1}$ and every closed unbounded subset $C$ of $\lambda$, there is $\eta\in C$ with the property that $\langle V_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ 
  and there is a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ into itself whose critical sequence consists of elements of $C$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Assume, towards a contradiction, that the above conclusion fails and let $\langle A,C\rangle$ be the least pair in the canonical well-ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}$ with the property that $A\in \textnormal{HOD}_{\lambda+1}$, $C$ is a closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ in $\textnormal{HOD}$ and for all $\eta\in C$ with the property that $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$, there is no  non-trivial elementary embedding of  $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ into itself  in $\textnormal{HOD}$ whose critical sequence consists of elements of $C$. 


    By our assumption, there is an ordinal $\zeta>\lambda$ such that $V_\zeta$ is sufficiently elementary in $V$, an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\zeta$ with $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}$ with $j(\lambda)=\lambda$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$. 
     
    Then $A,C\in X$ with $j(A)=A$ and $j(C)=C$. 
     
    Let $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j$. 

    \begin{claim*}
        $\kappa_n\in C$ for all $n<\omega$.
    \end{claim*}

    \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
      Since there exists an $n<\omega$ with $C\cap\kappa_n\neq\emptyset$, we can use the fact that $j(C)=C$ holds to conclude that $C\cap\kappa_0\neq\emptyset$. Then $\kappa_0\in C$, because otherwise we would have $\sup(C\cap\kappa_n)=\sup(C\cap\kappa_0)<\kappa_0$ for all $n<\omega$ and it would follow that $C$ is bounded in $\lambda$. We can now inductively conclude that $\kappa_n$ is an element of $C$ for all $n<\omega$. 
    \end{proof}


  \begin{claim*}
      If $n<\omega$, then $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_n},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_n}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$. 
  \end{claim*}

  \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
    Note that, since $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and $V_\zeta$ was chosen to be  sufficiently elementary in $V$, we have $\textnormal{HOD}_\eta\in X$ with $j(\textnormal{HOD}_\eta)=\textnormal{HOD}_{j(\eta)}$ for all $\eta\leq\lambda$. This implies that for all $\eta\leq\lambda$, the map $j\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\eta$ is an elementary embedding of $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ into $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_{j(\eta)},\in,A\cap V_{j(\eta)}\rangle$. In particular, it follows that $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_0},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_0}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_1},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_1}\rangle$ and, in combination with our first observation,  this inductively implies that $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_n},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_n}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_{n+1}},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_{n+1}}\rangle$ for all $n<\omega$. This conclusion implies the statement of the claim. 
   \end{proof}


    \begin{claim*}
     $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\eta\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\eta<\lambda$. 
    \end{claim*}

    \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
      Fix a cardinal $\eta<\lambda$. By our assumption, there exists a regular cardinal $(2^\eta)^+<\delta<\lambda$ that is not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$. Since $(2^\eta)^\textnormal{HOD}<\delta$, it follows that $\textnormal{HOD}$ contains a partition $\vec{S}=\langle{S_\gamma}~\vert~{\gamma<\eta}\rangle$ of $E^\delta_\omega$ into $\eta$-many  sets that are all stationary in $V$. Then $\vec{S}\in V_\lambda\subseteq X$. Set $j(\vec{S})=\langle{T_\gamma}~\vert~{\gamma<j(\delta)}\rangle$. Then $j(\delta)$ is a regular cardinal below $\lambda$ and $j(\vec{S})\in\textnormal{HOD}$ is a partition of $E^{j(\delta)}_\omega$ into $j(\eta)$-many stationary sets.  

      Now, set $\rho=\sup(j[\delta])<j(\delta)$. A result of Solovay in \cite{MR0379200} then shows that $$j[\eta] ~ = ~ \{{\gamma<j(\eta)}~\vert~{\textit{$T_\gamma\cap\rho$ is stationary in $\rho$}}\}.$$ 
       
      Since $j(\vec{S})$ is an element of $\textnormal{HOD}$, it follows that the set $j[\eta]$ is ordinal definable and this implies that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\eta$ is ordinal definable, because this function is the inverse of the transitive collapse of $j[\eta]$.  
          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    \end{proof}

    
    \begin{claim*}
     $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\textnormal{HOD}_\eta\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\eta<\lambda$. 
    \end{claim*}

    \begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
      Let $\lhd$ denote the ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}_\lambda$ that is obtained by first  ordering sets by their rank and then ordering  sets of the same rank using the canonical well-ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}$. Then $\lhd$ is an element of $\textnormal{HOD}$. Moreover, if $\delta<\lambda$ is  an inaccessible cardinal, then $\textnormal{HOD}_\delta$ is the initial segment of $\lhd$ of order-type $\delta$. For each such cardinal $\delta$, we let $${\pi_\delta}:{\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\delta,\lhd\rangle}\longrightarrow{\langle\delta,<\rangle}$$ denote the corresponding transitive collapse. Then $\pi_\delta\in\textnormal{HOD}\cap X$ with $j(\pi_\delta)=\pi_{j(\delta)}$ and $$j\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\delta ~ = ~ \pi_{j(\delta)}^{{-}1} ~ \circ ~ (j\mathbin\upharpoonright\delta) ~ \circ ~ \pi_\delta$$ for all inaccessible $\delta<\lambda$. In combination, this shows that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\delta$ is an element of $\textnormal{HOD}$.  
    \end{proof}


  Working in $\textnormal{HOD}$, we define $T$ to be set of all partial elementary embeddings $${i}:{\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle}\xrightarrow{part}{\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle}$$ with the property that there exists a natural number $n$ and a strictly increasing sequence $\langle{\mu_m}~\vert~{m\leq n+1}\rangle$ of elements of $C$ such that $\mathop{\mathrm{dom}}\nolimits(i)=V_{\mu_n}\cup\{\mu_n\}$, $i\mathbin\upharpoonright\mu_0=\operatorname{id}_{\mu_0}$,  $i(\mu_m)=\mu_{m+1}$ for all $m\leq n$ and $\langle V_{\mu_m},\in,A\cap V_{\mu_m}\rangle$ is an elementary submodel of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ for all $m\leq n+1$. By ordering $T$ under extensions, we can view this set as a tree of height at most $\omega$. 

  Since $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\textnormal{HOD}_\lambda$ is an elementary embedding of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ into itself, it follows that for all $n<\omega$, the sequence $\langle{\kappa_m}~\vert~{m\leq n+1}\rangle$ witnesses that the function $j\mathbin\upharpoonright(\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_n}\cup\{\kappa_n\})$ is an element of $T$. 
   
  In particular, there is a cofinal branch through $T$ in $V$ and we can use a well-foundedness argument to conclude that there is such a  branch $b$ in $\textnormal{HOD}$. The definition of $T$ now ensures that there is $\eta\in C$ with the property that $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ and   $\bigcup b$ is a non-trivial  elementary embedding of $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ into itself in $\textnormal{HOD}$ whose critical sequence consists of elements of $C$, contradicting our choice of $A$ and $C$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- claim--9: body_md -->
$\kappa_n\in C$ for all $n<\omega$.
<!-- end claim--9 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Since there exists an $n<\omega$ with $C\cap\kappa_n\neq\emptyset$, we can use the fact that $j(C)=C$ holds to conclude that $C\cap\kappa_0\neq\emptyset$. Then $\kappa_0\in C$, because otherwise we would have $\sup(C\cap\kappa_n)=\sup(C\cap\kappa_0)<\kappa_0$ for all $n<\omega$ and it would follow that $C$ is bounded in $\lambda$. We can now inductively conclude that $\kappa_n$ is an element of $C$ for all $n<\omega$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- claim--10: body_md -->
If $n<\omega$, then $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_n},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_n}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$.
<!-- end claim--10 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Note that, since $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and $V_\zeta$ was chosen to be  sufficiently elementary in $V$, we have $\textnormal{HOD}_\eta\in X$ with $j(\textnormal{HOD}_\eta)=\textnormal{HOD}_{j(\eta)}$ for all $\eta\leq\lambda$. This implies that for all $\eta\leq\lambda$, the map $j\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\eta$ is an elementary embedding of $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ into $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_{j(\eta)},\in,A\cap V_{j(\eta)}\rangle$. In particular, it follows that $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_0},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_0}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_1},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_1}\rangle$ and, in combination with our first observation,  this inductively implies that $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_n},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_n}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_{n+1}},\in,A\cap V_{\kappa_{n+1}}\rangle$ for all $n<\omega$. This conclusion implies the statement of the claim.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- claim--11: body_md -->
$j\mathbin\upharpoonright\eta\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\eta<\lambda$.
<!-- end claim--11 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Fix a cardinal $\eta<\lambda$. By our assumption, there exists a regular cardinal $(2^\eta)^+<\delta<\lambda$ that is not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$. Since $(2^\eta)^\textnormal{HOD}<\delta$, it follows that $\textnormal{HOD}$ contains a partition $\vec{S}=\langle{S_\gamma}~\vert~{\gamma<\eta}\rangle$ of $E^\delta_\omega$ into $\eta$-many  sets that are all stationary in $V$. Then $\vec{S}\in V_\lambda\subseteq X$. Set $j(\vec{S})=\langle{T_\gamma}~\vert~{\gamma<j(\delta)}\rangle$. Then $j(\delta)$ is a regular cardinal below $\lambda$ and $j(\vec{S})\in\textnormal{HOD}$ is a partition of $E^{j(\delta)}_\omega$ into $j(\eta)$-many stationary sets.  

      Now, set $\rho=\sup(j[\delta])<j(\delta)$. A result of Solovay in \cite{MR0379200} then shows that $$j[\eta] ~ = ~ \{{\gamma<j(\eta)}~\vert~{\textit{$T_\gamma\cap\rho$ is stationary in $\rho$}}\}.$$ 
       
      Since $j(\vec{S})$ is an element of $\textnormal{HOD}$, it follows that the set $j[\eta]$ is ordinal definable and this implies that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\eta$ is ordinal definable, because this function is the inverse of the transitive collapse of $j[\eta]$.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- claim--12: body_md -->
$j\mathbin\upharpoonright\textnormal{HOD}_\eta\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\eta<\lambda$.
<!-- end claim--12 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Let $\lhd$ denote the ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}_\lambda$ that is obtained by first  ordering sets by their rank and then ordering  sets of the same rank using the canonical well-ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}$. Then $\lhd$ is an element of $\textnormal{HOD}$. Moreover, if $\delta<\lambda$ is  an inaccessible cardinal, then $\textnormal{HOD}_\delta$ is the initial segment of $\lhd$ of order-type $\delta$. For each such cardinal $\delta$, we let $${\pi_\delta}:{\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\delta,\lhd\rangle}\longrightarrow{\langle\delta,<\rangle}$$ denote the corresponding transitive collapse. Then $\pi_\delta\in\textnormal{HOD}\cap X$ with $j(\pi_\delta)=\pi_{j(\delta)}$ and $$j\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\delta ~ = ~ \pi_{j(\delta)}^{{-}1} ~ \circ ~ (j\mathbin\upharpoonright\delta) ~ \circ ~ \pi_\delta$$ for all inaccessible $\delta<\lambda$. In combination, this shows that $j\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\delta$ is an element of $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- cor-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:ExactingStationaryLimitsHOD}
    Exacting cardinals are stationary limits of measurable cardinals in $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end cor-7 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
Let $\lambda$ be an exacting cardinal. Assume, towards a contradiction that the statement of the corollary fails and let $C$ be the least closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ in the canonical well-ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}$ whose elements are not measurable cardinals in $\textnormal{HOD}$. 

    First, assume that unboundedly many regular cardinals below $\lambda$ are not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$. Then Theorem \ref{theorem:ExactingInHOD} yields $\eta\in C$ and a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle\textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in\rangle$ into itself in $\textnormal{HOD}$ whose critical sequence consists of elements of $C$. We then know that $\operatorname{crit}(j)\in C$ is a measurable cardinal in $\textnormal{HOD}$. 

    Now, assume that eventually all regular cardinals below $\lambda$ are $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$. Pick $\zeta>\lambda$ such that $V_\zeta$ is sufficiently elementary in $V$ and use the exactingness of $\lambda$ to find an elementary submodel $X$ of $V_\zeta$ with $V_\lambda\cup\{\lambda\}\subseteq X$ and an elementary embedding ${j}:{X}\longrightarrow{V_\zeta}$ with $j\mathbin\upharpoonright\lambda\neq\operatorname{id}_\lambda$ and $j(\lambda)=\lambda$. 
     
    Let $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j$. 
    Our choice of $C$ then ensures that $C$ is an element of $X$ with $j(C)=C$ and we can repeat an argument from the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem:ExactingInHOD} to see that $\kappa_n\in C$ holds for all $n<\omega$. Since the critical sequence of $j$ consists of cardinals that are regular in $V$, our assumption yields an $n<\omega$ with the property that $\kappa_n$ is $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$. In particular, it follows that $\kappa_n$ is an element of $C$ that is a measurable cardinal in $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- cor-8: body_md -->
\label{corollary:ExactingInHOD}
    Let $\lambda$ be an exacting cardinal with the property that the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis holds in $V_\lambda$, let $A\in\textnormal{HOD}_{\lambda+1}$ and let $C$ be a closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ in $\textnormal{HOD}$. 
      Then, in $\textnormal{HOD}$, for every $A\in V_{\lambda+1}$ and every closed unbounded subset $C$ of $\lambda$, there is $\eta\in C$ with the property that $\langle V_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle V_\lambda,\in,A\rangle$ 
  and there is a non-trivial elementary embedding of $\langle V_\eta,\in,A\cap V_\eta\rangle$ into itself whose critical sequence consists of elements of $C$.
<!-- end cor-8 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
If $\kappa<\lambda$ is a cardinal that is not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$ in $V_\lambda$, then the fact that $\textnormal{HOD}^{V_\lambda}\subseteq\textnormal{HOD}$ holds ensures that $\kappa$ is not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$ in $V$. In particular, if the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis holds in $V_\lambda$, then there are  unboundedly many regular cardinals below $\lambda$ that are not $\omega$-strongly measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$. The desired conclusion now follows from an application of Theorem \ref{theorem:ExactingInHOD}.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Assume that the Weak $\textnormal{HOD}$ Conjecture is true and let $\lambda$ be an exacting cardinal. Then $\lambda$ is an inaccessible cardinal in $\textnormal{HOD}$. Moreover, since $V_\lambda$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$ with a huge cardinal above an extendible cardinal. Our assumption then implies that the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis holds in $V_\lambda$ and this directly yields \eqref{item:ExactingInHODIntro2} of the theorem. 

    For \eqref{item:ExactingInHODIntro1}, let $\Gamma\in \textnormal{HOD}_{\lambda+1}\setminus V_\lambda$ be a set of graphs and let $C\in\textnormal{HOD}$ be the closed unbounded subset of $\lambda$ consisting of the limits of ranks of graphs in $\Gamma$. An application of Corollary \ref{corollary:ExactingInHOD} now yields a non-trivial elementary embedding $j$ of $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\eta,\in,\Gamma\cap V_\eta\rangle$ into itself in $\textnormal{HOD}$ for some $\eta\in C$. By the definition of $\Gamma$, there exists a graph $\mathcal{G}$ in $\Gamma\cap V_\eta$ whose rank is greater than the critical point of $j$. Since $\eta$ is the least non-trivial fixed point of $j$, it follows that $\mathcal{G}\neq j(\mathcal{G})\in \Gamma$ and $j$ induced an embedding of $\mathcal{G}$ into $j(\mathcal{G})$. Since $\lambda$ is inaccessible in $\textnormal{HOD}$, these computations show that $\lambda$ is a Vop\v{e}nka cardinal in $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{theorem:RankIntoRankInHOD}
    Let ${j}:{V_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}$ be a $\Sigma^1_4$-correct I3-embedding and let $A\in\textnormal{HOD}_{\lambda+1}$. If the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis holds in $V_{\bar{\lambda}}$ for all $\bar{\lambda}<\lambda$ with the property that there exists an I3-embedding from $V_{\bar{\lambda}}$ to itself, then $\lambda$ is a limit of ordinals $\alpha$ such that, in $\textnormal{HOD}$, there is a non-trivial elementary embedding of the structure $\langle V_\alpha,\in,A\cap V_\alpha\rangle$ into itself.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Fix $\xi<\lambda$. Using {\cite[Theorem 2.4]{La97}}, we can find a $\Sigma^1_4$-correct I3-embedding ${j^\prime}:{V_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}$ with $\operatorname{crit}(j^\prime)>\xi$. Let $\vec{\kappa}=\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j^\prime$. We then know that $j^\prime$ can be extended to an I2-embedding that is given by a $(\kappa_0,\lambda)$-extender $E$. Let $$\langle\langle{M_\alpha}~\vert~{\alpha\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle,\langle{{j^\prime_{\alpha,\beta}}:{M_\alpha}\longrightarrow{M_\beta}}~\vert~{\alpha\leq\beta\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle\rangle$$ denote the iteration of $V$ and $E$ and set $A^\prime=j^\prime_{0,\omega}(A\cap V_{\kappa_0})$. Then $A\cap\kappa_0=A^\prime\cap\kappa_0$ and Proposition \ref{proposition:IterationFixedPoints}\eqref{prop:InvEmb2} ensures that $j^\prime_+(A^\prime)=j^\prime_{0,1}(A^\prime)=A^\prime$. 
   
  In addition, let $\lhd$ denote the ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}_{\kappa_0}$ that is obtained by first  ordering sets by their rank and then ordering  sets of the same rank  using the canonical well-ordering of $\textnormal{HOD}$. Set ${\blacktriangleleft}=j_{0,\omega}(\lhd)$. Then ${\blacktriangleleft}\cap V_{\kappa_0}=\lhd$ and $j^\prime_+({\blacktriangleleft})=j^\prime_{0,1}({\blacktriangleleft})={\blacktriangleleft}$. 
  
  Iterated applications of {\cite[Theorem 2.4]{La97}} now allow us to find a sequence $\langle{{i_m}:{V_\lambda}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}}~\vert~{m<\omega}\rangle$ of $\Sigma^1_2$-correct I3-embeddings with the property that the sequence $\langle{\operatorname{crit}(i_m)}~\vert~{m<\omega}\rangle$ is strictly increasing in the interval $(\xi,\kappa_0)$ and for all $m<\omega$, the critical sequence of $i_m$ is equal to $\langle\operatorname{crit}(i_n)\rangle^\smallfrown\vec{\kappa}$,  $(i_m)_+(A^\prime)=A^\prime$, $(i_m)_+({\blacktriangleleft})={\blacktriangleleft}$, $i_m(\operatorname{crit}(i_m))=\kappa_0$ and $i_m(\kappa_n)=\kappa_{n+1}$ for all $n<\omega$. Define  $$\bar{\lambda} ~ = ~ \sup_{n<\omega}\operatorname{crit}(i_n) ~ \in ~ (\xi,\kappa_0).$$ 
  
  An inverse limit construction (see {\cite[Section 3]{La97}}) now yields an elementary  embedding ${i}:{V_{\bar{\lambda}}}\longrightarrow{V_\lambda}$ with critical sequence $\langle{\operatorname{crit}(i_n)}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ and $i(\operatorname{crit}(i_n))=\kappa_n$ for all $n<\omega$. We can then extend $i$ to a map ${i_+}:{V_{\bar{\lambda}+1}}\longrightarrow{V_{\lambda+1}}$ by setting $$i_+(B) ~ = ~ \bigcup\{{i(B\cap V_{\operatorname{crit}(i_n)})}~\vert~{n<\omega}\}$$ for all $B\in V_{\bar{\lambda}+1}$. Our setup then ensures that $$i_+(A\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}) ~ = ~ i_+(A^\prime\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}) ~ = ~ A^\prime$$ and $$i_+({\lhd}\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}) ~ = ~ i_+({\blacktriangleleft}\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}) ~ = ~ {\blacktriangleleft}.$$ 
   
  Using {\cite[Theorem 3.3]{La97}}, we can now find an I3-embedding ${k}:{V_{\bar{\lambda}}}\longrightarrow{V_{\bar{\lambda}}}$ with critical sequence $\langle{\operatorname{crit}(i_n)}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ satisfying $$k_+(A\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}) ~ = ~ A\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}$$ and $$k_+({\lhd}\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}) ~ = ~ {\lhd}\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}.$$ 
  
  Note that, since $\textnormal{HOD}_{\bar{\lambda}}$ is the initial segment of $\lhd$ of order-type $\bar{\lambda}$, we also know that $k_+(\textnormal{HOD}_{\bar{\lambda}}) = \textnormal{HOD}_{\bar{\lambda}}$. In particular, it follows that for all $\alpha<\bar{\lambda}$, the map  $k\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\alpha$ is a non-trivial elementary embedding of the structure $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\alpha,\in,A\cap V_\alpha\rangle$ into the structure $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_{k(\alpha)},\in,A\cap V_{k(\alpha)}\rangle$. Given $n<\omega$, we then know that $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_{\operatorname{crit}(i_n)},\in,A\cap V_{\operatorname{crit}(i_n)}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_{\bar{\lambda}},\in,A\cap V_\lambda\rangle$. 

  Since our assumptions ensure that the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis holds in $V_{\bar{\lambda}}$, we can repeat the corresponding argument from the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem:ExactingInHOD} to obtain the following statement: 

 \begin{claim*}
     $k\mathbin\upharpoonright\alpha\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\alpha<\bar{\lambda}$. \qed 
 \end{claim*}  

 If $\delta<\bar{\lambda}$ is an inaccessible cardinal, then $\textnormal{HOD}_\delta$ is the initial segment of $\lhd$ or order-type $\delta$. Given such a cardinal $\delta$, we let $${\pi_\delta}:{\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\delta,\lhd\rangle}\longrightarrow{\langle\delta,<\rangle}$$ denote the corresponding transitive collapse. The above computations now that $k(\pi_\delta)=\pi_{k(\delta)}$ holds. This allows us to repeat another argument from the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem:ExactingInHOD} and derive the following statement: 

  \begin{claim*}
     $k\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\alpha\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\alpha<\bar{\lambda}$. \qed 
 \end{claim*}  

 Now, in $\textnormal{HOD}$, we define $T$ to be set of all partial elementary embeddings $${\ell}:{\langle V_{\bar{\lambda}},\in,A\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}\rangle}\xrightarrow{part}{\langle V_{\bar{\lambda}},\in,A\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}\rangle}$$ with the property that there exists a natural number $n$ and a strictly increasing sequence $\langle{\mu_m}~\vert~{m\leq n+2}\rangle$ of ordinals below $\bar{\lambda}$ such that $\mathop{\mathrm{dom}}\nolimits(\ell)=V_{\mu_{n+1}}$, ${{\rm{ran}}(\ell)}=V_{\mu_{n+2}}$, $\ell\mathbin\upharpoonright\mu_0=\operatorname{id}_{\mu_0}$,  $\ell(\mu_m)=\mu_{m+1}$ for all $m\leq n$ and the structure $\langle V_{\mu_m},\in,A\cap V_{\mu_m}\rangle$ is an elementary substructure of $\langle V_{\bar{\lambda}},\in,A\cap V_{\bar{\lambda}}\rangle$ for all $m\leq n+2$. 
  
 Ordering the elements of  $T$ under extensions then turns this set into a tree of height at most $\omega$. Moreover, for all $n<\omega$, the function $k\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_{\operatorname{crit}(n+1)}$ is an element of $T$. This shows that $T$ has a cofinal branch in $V$ and hence this tree has a cofinal branch $b$ in $\textnormal{HOD}$. In this situation, there exists an ordinal $\xi<\alpha\leq\bar{\lambda}$ with the property that $\bigcup b$ is a non-trivial elementary embedding of the structure $\langle \textnormal{HOD}_\alpha,\in,A\cap V_\alpha\rangle$ into itself in $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- claim--13: body_md -->
$k\mathbin\upharpoonright\alpha\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\alpha<\bar{\lambda}$. \qed
<!-- end claim--13 -->
<!-- claim--14: body_md -->
$k\mathbin\upharpoonright \textnormal{HOD}_\alpha\in\textnormal{HOD}$ for all $\alpha<\bar{\lambda}$. \qed
<!-- end claim--14 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{theorem:ConstructionSuccOfExactingExtendibleInZF}
  Assume that ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$ is an I2-embedding with least non-trivial fixed point $\lambda$ and the $\mathrm{CCA}$ holds in  $V_\lambda$. Then there is a transitive set $N$ such that $V_\lambda\in N$ and the following statements hold: 
 \begin{enumerate}
   \item  $N$ is a model of $\mathrm{ZF}+\textsf{\textup{DC}}_{{<}\lambda}$. 
   
     \item  $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $N$. 
                                                                                             
     \item $\lambda^+$ is an extendible cardinal in $\textnormal{HOD}_x^N$ for all  $x\in \mathcal{P}(\lambda)^N$.
 \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Let $\langle{\kappa_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ denote the critical sequence of $j$. Then $\kappa=\kappa_0$ and $\lambda=\sup_{n<\omega}\kappa_n$. 
  
 Without loss of generality, we may also assume that $j$ is given by a $(\kappa,\lambda)$-extender $E$ and, as outlined above, we can consider the iteration $$\langle \langle{M_\alpha}~\vert~{\alpha\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle,\langle{{j_{\alpha,\beta}}:{M_\alpha}\longrightarrow{M_\beta}}~\vert~{\alpha\leq\beta\in\operatorname{Ord}}\rangle\rangle$$ of $V$ and $E$. Let $\kappa <\mu <j(\kappa)$ be an extendible cardinal in $V_\lambda$ and let ${\mathcal{U}}$ be the normal, ${<}\kappa$-complete, fine ultrafilter on $\mathcal{P}_\kappa(\mu)$ induced by $j$. In addition, let $\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}}$ be the corresponding {Supercompact Prikry forcing} (see \S\ref{sec: Supercompact Prikry}).

\smallskip

Define $\vec{x}=\langle{x_n}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$ to be the unique sequence with $$x_n ~  = ~ j_{n,\omega}[j_{0,n}(\mu)]$$ for all $n<\omega$.\footnote{Note that $j_{n,n+1}[j_{0,n}(\mu)]$ equals $[\operatorname{id}]_{j_{0,n}(\mathcal{U})}$.}
                                                                                                                                        


\begin{claim*}
    The sequence $\vec{x}$ is $\prec$-increasing in $\mathcal{P}_\lambda(j_{0,\omega}(\mu))$ and for each $A\in j_{0,\omega}({\mathcal{U}})$, there is an $n_*<\omega$ with the property that $x_n\in A$ for all $n\geq n_*$.\qed
\end{claim*}


By the Mathias criterion of genericity for Supercompact Prikry forcing (see \cite[\S1]{Gitik-handbook}), the sequence $\vec{x}$ induces a $j_{0,\omega}({\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}})$-generic filter $$G(\vec{x}) ~ = ~ \{{\langle s, A\rangle\in j_{0,\omega}({\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}})}~\vert~{s\sqsubseteq \vec{x}, ~ \vec{x}\setminus s\subseteq A}\}$$ over $M_\omega$. 
 
Clearly, we have $M_\omega[\vec{x}]=M_\omega[G(\vec{x})]$ and  $|j_{0,\omega}({\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}})|^{M_\omega}<j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)$. 
 
In particular, it follows that $(M_{\omega})_{j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)}[\vec{x}]=M_\omega[\vec{x}]_{j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)}$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$. 
 
Define $$\bar{M} ~ = ~ (M_\omega)_{j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)}.$$ Elementarity then ensures that $\bar{M}$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}+``V=\textnormal{gHOD}"$ and $j_{0,\omega}(\mu)$ is extendible in $\bar{M}$.\footnote{In \cite{ABLG}, the authors  looked at the generic extension of $\bar{M}$ via the Prikry sequence induced by $j$. The natural analogue here would be to look at the generic extension $\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$. The caveat, though, is that the $\bar{M}$-cardinal $j_{0,\omega}(\mu)$ is collapsed to $\lambda$ when passing from $\bar{M}$  to $\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$. So instead, we will look at the $\textnormal{ZF}$-submodel of $\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$ given by all the objects that are  definable (in $\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$) from parameters in $\bar{M}$ and from subsets of $\lambda$ in the various sub-generic extensions of $\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$.} Moreover, we have $V_\lambda\in\bar{M}$. 


Define  $\mathcal{R}$ to be the collection of all $\bar{M}$-regular cardinals in the interval $[\lambda,j_{0,\omega}(\mu))$  and for each  $\alpha\in \mathcal{R}$, define $${\pi_\alpha}:{\mathcal{P}_\lambda(j_{0,\omega}(\mu))}\longrightarrow{\mathcal{P}_\lambda(\alpha)}; ~ x\mapsto x\cap \alpha$$ to be the map  that induces a Rudin--Keisler projection of $j_{0,\omega}({\mathcal{U}})$ that we denote by  $j_{0,\omega}(\mathcal{U})_\alpha$. 
 
By the Mathias criterion of genericity, the sequence  $$\vec{x}_\alpha  ~ = ~ \langle{x_n\cap\alpha}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$$ is ${\mathbb{P}}_{j_{0,\omega}({\mathcal{U}})_\alpha}$-generic over $\bar{M}$. 

              
                                                                                                                                      
            
                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
             
\smallskip

Following arguments of Kafkoulis in \cite{Kafkoulis}, our intended model is $$N ~ = ~ \bar{M}\big(\bigcup\{{\mathcal{P}^{\bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha]}(\lambda)}~\vert~{\alpha\in \mathcal{R}}\}\big).$$ 


The following statements are all proven by Kafkoulis in \cite{Kafkoulis}: 


\begin{claim*}                        
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item\label{item:Kafkoulis1} $N$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZF}+\textsf{\textup{DC}}_{{<}\lambda}$. 
        
        \item\label{item:Kafkoulis2} Every set of ordinals in $N$ belongs to $\bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha]$ for some $\alpha\in \mathcal{R}$. 
        
        \item\label{item:Kafkoulis3} $\lambda$ is a strong limit cardinal of countable cofinality in $N$ and $j_{0,\omega}(\mu)=(\lambda^+)^N$. 
        
        \item\label{item:Kafkoulis4} The following statements are equivalent for every $\theta <\lambda$: 
          \begin{enumerate}
              \item $\theta$ is an $N$-cardinal. 

              \item $\theta$ is an $\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$-cardinal. 

              \item $\theta$ is an $\bar{M}$-cardinal.
          \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate}
\end{claim*}

\begin{proof}[Proof of the claim]
    \eqref{item:Kafkoulis1}  is {\cite[Corollary 4.1.13]{Kafkoulis}},  
    \eqref{item:Kafkoulis2}  is {\cite[Corollary 2.1.12]{Kafkoulis}},   \eqref{item:Kafkoulis3} is \cite[Corollary 2.1.13]{Kafkoulis} and \eqref{item:Kafkoulis4} follows from the fact that forcing with $j_{0,\omega}({\mathbb{P}}_{{\mathcal{U}}})$ does not add bounded subsets to $\lambda$. 
\end{proof}


\begin{claim*}
    $j\mathbin\upharpoonright N$ is an elementary embedding of $N$ into itself. 
\end{claim*}

\begin{proof}[Proof of claim]
  Since $N$ is a set-sized model and ${j}:{V}\longrightarrow{M}$ is an elementary embedding, it is clear that ${j\mathbin\upharpoonright N}:{N}\longrightarrow{j(N)}$ is also an elementary embedding. Thus, it suffices to argue that $j(N)=N$ holds.  To show this, we first observe the  following: 
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $j(\bar{M})=j((M_\omega)_{j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)})=(M_\omega)_{j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)}$. 
    
    \item $j(\mathcal{R})=\mathcal{R}$. 
    
    \item $j(\vec{x})_\alpha=\langle{j(x_n)\cap\alpha}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle=\langle{x_{n+1}\cap\alpha}~\vert~{n<\omega}\rangle$.\footnote{In particular, we have $\bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha]=\bar{M}[j(\vec{x})_\alpha]$, because $x_0=x_{1}\cap \sup(x_0)$.}
  \end{itemize}

 The set $N$ is the smallest $\textnormal{ZF}$-model containing $\bar{M}$ that has the set $$\bigcup\{{\mathcal{P}^{\bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha]}(\lambda)}~\vert~{\alpha\in \mathcal{R}}\}$$ as an element. By elementarity, in $M$, the set $j(N)$ is  the smallest $\textnormal{ZF}$-model containing $j\big(\bar{M})=\bar{M}$ that has $$j(\bigcup\{{\mathcal{P}^{\bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha]}(\lambda)}~\vert~{\alpha\in \mathcal{R}}\}\big) ~ = ~ \bigcup\{{\mathcal{P}^{\bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha]}(\lambda)}~\vert~{\alpha\in \mathcal{R}}\}$$ as an element. In particular, we have $j(N)=N$, as needed.
\end{proof}


We now know that $N\subseteq M$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZF}$, $V_\lambda\in N$, ${{\rm{cof}}(\lambda)}^N=\omega$ and $j\mathbin\upharpoonright N$ is an elementary embedding of $N$ into $N$. Moreover, since $V_\lambda\in N$ is a model of $\mathrm{CCA}$ and therefore $"V=\textnormal{HOD}"$ holds in $V_\lambda$,  there is a well-ordering of $V_\lambda$ in $N$. 
 
Invoking Corollary~\ref{corollary:ExactingInnerModel}, we can  conclude that  $\lambda$ is an  exacting cardinal in $N$.

\smallskip

Finally, we analyze $\textnormal{HOD}^N_x$ for an arbitrary set $x\in \mathcal{P}^N(\lambda)$: 


\begin{claim*}
    For each $x\in \mathcal{P}^N(\lambda)$ there is $\alpha\in \mathcal{R}$ such that $$\bar{M}\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}^N_x\subseteq \bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha].$$
\end{claim*}

\begin{proof}[Proof of claim]
   To prove the first inclusion, it suffices to show that every set of ordinals in $\bar{M}$ belongs to $\textnormal{HOD}^N_x$. Since every set of ordinals in $\bar{M}$ was coded into the continuum-function-pattern cofinally often  below $j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)$ and $|j_{0,\omega}(\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}})|<j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)$, this coding is absolute between $\bar{M}$ and $N$. In particular, we have  $$\bar{M} ~ \subseteq  ~ \textnormal{HOD}^N ~ \subseteq ~ \textnormal{HOD}^N_x.$$ 

   For the second  inclusion, since $\bar{M}\subseteq \textnormal{HOD}^N_x\subseteq \bar{M}[\vec{x}]$, the intermediate model theorem hands us a generic filter $H\in\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$ for a subforcing of $j_{0,\omega} (\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}})$ such that $\bar{M}[H]=\textnormal{HOD}^N_x$. Since the latter is a model of choice, there is a set of ordinals $A\in N$ such that $\bar{M}[H]=\bar{M}[A]$. Invoking \eqref{item:Kafkoulis2} from our second claim,  we find $\alpha\in \mathcal{R}$ such that $A\in \bar{M}[\vec x_\alpha]$, hence $\textnormal{HOD}^N_x\subseteq \bar{M}[\vec{x}_\alpha]$, as needed. 
\end{proof}

By the intermediate model theorem $\textnormal{HOD}^N_x$ is a generic extension by a subforcing of $\mathrm{RO}(j_{0,\omega}(\mathbb{P})_{\pi_\alpha(j_{0,\omega}(\mathcal{U}))})$, hence by a forcing of size less than $j_{0,\omega}(\mu)$. As a result, the latter is an extendible cardinal in $\textnormal{HOD}^N_x$.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- claim--15: body_md -->
The sequence $\vec{x}$ is $\prec$-increasing in $\mathcal{P}_\lambda(j_{0,\omega}(\mu))$ and for each $A\in j_{0,\omega}({\mathcal{U}})$, there is an $n_*<\omega$ with the property that $x_n\in A$ for all $n\geq n_*$.\qed
<!-- end claim--15 -->

        \item\label{item:Kafkoulis3} $\lambda$ is a strong limit cardinal of countable cofinality in $N$ and $j_{0,\omega}(\mu)=(\lambda^+)^N$.

          \begin{enumerate}
              \item $\theta$ is an $N$-cardinal. 

              \item $\theta$ is an $\bar{M}[\vec{x}]$-cardinal. 

              \item $\theta$ is an $\bar{M}$-cardinal.
          \end{enumerate} 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end claim--16 -->

Since every set of ordinals in $\bar{M}$ was coded into the continuum-function-pattern cofinally often  below $j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)$ and $|j_{0,\omega}(\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{U}})|<j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)$, this coding is absolute between $\bar{M}$ and $N$. <!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{thm:generalizingABLG}
   Assume the  hypothesis of Theorem \ref{theorem:ConstructionSuccOfExactingExtendibleInZF}. Then there is a transitive, set-sized model $\bar{M}$ of $\textnormal{ZFC}$ with $V_\lambda\in\bar{M}$ and an ordinal $\lambda<\bar{\mu}\in\bar{M}$ with the property that for every $\lambda<\alpha<\bar{\mu}$, there exists a transitive set $M(\alpha)$ such that $M(\alpha)$ is a forcing extension of $\bar{M}$, $\lambda$ is an exacting cardinal in $M(\alpha)$, $\bar{\mu}$ is an extendible cardinal in $M(\alpha)$ and $\alpha<(\lambda^+)^{M(\alpha)}$.
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
We use the notations of the proof of Theorem~\ref{theorem: exacting + extendible} and again define $\bar{M}=(M_\omega)_{j_{0,\omega}(\lambda)}$. Set $\bar{\mu}=j_{0,\omega}(\mu)$. Given $\lambda<\alpha<\bar{\mu}$, pick $\alpha\leq\beta\in\mathcal{R}$ and define $M(\alpha)=\bar{M}[\vec{x}_\beta]$. 
     
    The above arguments then show that $\bar{\mu}$ is an extendible cardinal in $M(\alpha)$. Moreover, Corollary~\ref{corollary:ExactingInnerModel} ensures that $\lambda$ is exacting in $M(\alpha)$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
If $\mathrm{ZFC}$ is consistent with the existence of an ultraexacting cardinal, then the resulting theory does not prove that a proper class of ordinals are measurable in $\textnormal{HOD}$.
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem 4.5]{ABLG}, the consistency of $\mathrm{ZFC}$ with an ultraexacting cardinal implies the consistency of $\mathrm{ZFC}$ with an I0-embedding. Work in a model of $\mathrm{ZFC}$ with an I0-embedding ${j}:{V_{\lambda+1}}\longrightarrow{V_{\lambda+1}}$ and let $G$ be ${\rm{Add}}({\lambda^+},{1})$-generic over $V$. Then $L(V_{\lambda+1})[G]$ is a model of $\mathrm{ZFC}$ and \cite[Corollary 3.31]{ABL} shows that $\lambda$ is an ultraexacting cardinal in this model. Classical results of Vop\v{e}nka (see \cite[Theorem~6]{MR3821636}) now show that $L(V_{\lambda+1})[G]$ is a forcing extension of $\textnormal{HOD}^{L(V_{\lambda+1})[G]}$ using a set-sized partial order and, since $L(V_{\lambda+1})[G]$ does not contain a proper class of measurable cardinals, it follows that $\textnormal{HOD}^{L(V_{\lambda+1})[G]}$ does not contain a proper class of measurable cardinals.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- question-5: body_md -->
\label{que:isWHODHnecessary}
  Assuming the consistency of $\textnormal{ZF}$ with some large cardinal axioms that is not known to be inconsistent, is it possible to show that $\textnormal{ZFC}$ is consistent with the existence of a cardinal  $\lambda$ of uncountable cofinality  with the property that $\mathop{1\hskip-3pt {\rm l}}\Vdash_{\mathbb{P}}\textit{$``\check{\lambda}$ is an exacting cardinal }"$ holds for some  partial order ${\mathbb{P}}\in H(\lambda)$?
<!-- end question-5 -->
<!-- question-6: body_md -->
If the $\textnormal{HOD}$ Hypothesis is true, is every exacting cardinal weakly compact in $\textnormal{HOD}$?
<!-- end question-6 -->
<!-- question-7: body_md -->
Does the existence of an exacting cardinal imply the existence of an I3-embedding in $\textnormal{HOD}$?
<!-- end question-7 -->
<!-- question-8: body_md -->
Does the existence of an I1-embedding imply the existence of an I3-embedding in $\textnormal{HOD}$? If so, does this conclusion also follow from the existence of an I2- or I3-embedding?
<!-- end question-8 -->
<!-- question-9: body_md -->
Is there a version of  Theorem~\ref{theorem: exacting + extendible}  where $N$ is a model of $\textnormal{ZFC}$?
<!-- end question-9 -->
